Reli-gious rite: उपवास: Aṅgiras told Bhīṣma that if one, with controlled sense organs, spent the month of Vaiśākha eating only once a day (निस्तरेद् एकभक्तेन वैशाखम्), whether he be a man or a woman, became eminent among his kinsmen 13. 109. 23. C. Use in a Simile: Description of a “Brah-macārī” who visited Ṛśyaśṛṅga's hermitage: just as the forest, in the month of Mādhava (माधवमासि), when stirred by the wind, wafts (fragrance), so does ‘he’, when attended by wind, emits (fragrance) 3. 112. 8.
वंशगुल्म: Vaṃśagulma m.: Name of a तीर्थ। It is the source of the rivers Śoṇa and Narmadā (शोणस्य नर्मदायाश् च प्र-भवे … । वंशगुल्मे); by bathing there (उपस्पृश्य) one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice (Vājimedha) 3. 83. 9.
वंशमूलक: Vaṃśamūlaka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By reaching it (आसाद्य) and by bathing there a pilgrim (तीर्थसेवी) lifts up his family 3. 81. 34.
वक्रद्वार: Vakradvāra m.: Name of a mountain. One of the three mountains, the other two being Droṇa and Śataśṛṅga, piled up together by Indra for the सत्रस् of the ance-stors of Sulabhā (द्रोणश् च शतशृङ्गश् च वक्रद्वारश् च पर्वतः । मम सत्रेषु पूर्वेषाम् चिता मघवता सह ॥ ) 12. 308. 183 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 320. 182: द्रोणा-दयः पर्वताः मम पूर्वेषां सत्रेषु मघवता सह चिताः चयने इष्टकास्थाने निवेशिता इत्य् अर्थः).
वङ्क्षु: Vaṅkṣu f.: Name of a river. Listed by Bhīṣma in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 17, 2.
वटेश्वरपुर: Vaṭeśvarapura nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Sacred to Keśava (Kṛṣṇa); by reaching (गत्वा) Vaṭeśvarapura, by worshipping Keśava there, and by observing fast (उपवासात्) one undoubtedly gets the desired objects (ईप्सितान्  … कामान्) 3. 82. 111.
वधूसरा: Vadhūsarā f.: Name of a river. Flowing by the आश्रम of Cyavana (च्यवनस्याश्रमं प्रति) 1. 6. 7; described as a great river (महानदी) 1. 6. 6; a river arose from the tears flowing from the eyes of Pulomā, wife of Bhṛgu; the river followed the step of Pulomā; seeing that, Pitāmaha (Brahman) named the river Vadhū-sarā (अश्रुबिन्दूद्भवा तस्याः प्रावर्तत महानदी । … तस्या मार्गं सृतवतीं दृष्ट्वा तु सरितं तदा । नाम तस्यास् तदा नद्याश् चक्रे लोकपितामहः वधूसरेति) 1. 6. 6-7.
वन्दना: Vandanā f.: Name of a river. Described as a great river (महानदी): listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drink-ing 6. 10. 17, 13 (for other details see Puṣpa-veṇī).
वरदा: Varadā f.: Name of a river. If one bathes at the confluence of Varadā (वरदासंगमे) one gets the fruit of gift-ing a thousand cows 3. 83. 31.
वरदान: Varadāna nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One can reach this तीर्थ from the place where Sarasvatī meets the ocean 3. 80. 79; by bathing at this तीर्थ one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 80. 81; sage Durvāsas gave here a boon to Viṣṇu (विष्णोर् दुर्वाससा यत्र वरो दत्तः) 3. 80. 81.
वराणसी: Varāṇasī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 30, 13 (for other details see Puṣpaveṇī).
वराह: Varāha1 m.: Name of a mountain. Described as having big summits (महा-शृङ्ग) 2. 19. 2; one of the five mountains —the other four being Vaihāra, Vṛṣabha, Ṛṣigiri and Caityaka—surrounding the city Girivraja in the Magadha country; the five mountains came together as though for pro-tecting the city (एते पञ्चमहाशृङ्गाः पर्-वताः … । रक्षन्तीवाभिसंहत्य संह-ताङ्गा गिरिव्रजम् ॥ ) 2. 19. 2-3 (for other details see Ṛṣigīri). [See Varāha2]

Varāha2 m.: Name of a mountain. So called because Vṛṣākapi (Nārāyaṇa), after assuming the form of a boar and after lifting up the lost earth (इमां हि धरणीं पूर्वं नष्टाम् … गोविन्द उज्जहाराशु वाराहं रूपम् आश्रितः 12. 333. 11) offered पिण्डस् on the Varāha mountain with all detailed rites to his father, grandfather and great-grandfather and worshipped himself; he then disappeared instantly 12. 333. 22.
वरुणस्रोतस: Varuṇasrotasa m.: Name of a moun-tain. In the south (दक्षिणस्याम्) 3. 86. 1; on this mountain (वरुणस्रोतसे गिरौ) there is the forest of Māṭhara and his sacri-ficial post (यूप) 3. 86. 7.
वरुणह्रद: Varuṇahrada m.: Name of a lake. The lake of Varuṇa in the Nāgaloka below the earth (5. 96. 6, 8); fire in big flames is wide awake there (अग्निर् एष महा-र्चिष्मान् जागर्ति वरुणह्रदे) 5. 96. 18.
वसिष्ठस्य: Vasiṣṭhasya parvataḥ m.: Designation of a mountain. On the lower range of the Himavant (हिमवत्पार्श्वम् 1. 207. 1); Arjuna visited it during his exile 1. 207. 2.

Vasiṣṭhasya āśramaḥ1 m.: The आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha. A. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 1. 165. 1. B. Past event: Viśvāmitra, when out for hunting and thirsty, happened to reach the आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha (मृगलिप्सुः पिपा-सितः । आजगाम … वसिष्ठस्याश्रमं प्रति) 1. 165. 6; when Viśvāmitra tried to take away Vasiṣṭha's cow Nandinī by force, she did not leave the आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha 1. 165. 23; enmity arose between Vasiṣṭha and Viśvāmitra when the latter stayed in the आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha (वैरं विश्वामित्र-वसिष्ठयोः । वसतोर् आश्रमे) 1. 165. 1.

Vasiṣṭhasya āśramaḥ3 m.: The आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha (identical with the above ?) A. Location: On the confluence of Niścīrā (निश्चीरासंगमे … तत्राश्रमो वसि-ष्ठस्य) 3. 82. 120-121. B. Description: Famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः) 3. 82. 121. C. Holiness: By bathing there one got the fruit of perform-ing a Vājapeya sacrifice (तत्राभिषेकं कुर्वाणो वाजपेयम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 82. 121.

Vasiṣṭhasya āśramaḥ3 m.: The आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha. A. Location: At Sthāṇutīrtha (also called Sarasvatītīrtha) on the eastern bank of the river Sarasvatī (आश्रमो वै वसिष्ठ-स्य स्थाणुतीर्थे ऽभवन् महान् । पूर्वतः) 9. 41. 4; (अपोवाह वसिष्ठं तु प्राचीं दिशम्) 9. 41. 34. B. Description: Great (महन्त्) 9. 41. 4. C. Past event: Sara-svatī carried away Vasiṣṭha from his आश्रम by withdrawing her bank near it (तेन कूलापहारेण मैत्रावरुणिर् औह्यत) to the other side (west) 9. 41. 27-28; later she carried him back to his side 9. 41. 34. [See Vasiṣṭhāpavāha Vol. 1. 438 and Sarasvatī (Past events 11) Vol. 1. 473-474]

Vasiṣṭhasya āśramaḥ4 m.: The आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha. A. Location: Near the western ocean (समुद्रं ते समाश्रित्य वारुणम् … काले-याः संप्रवर्तन्त) 3. 100. 1. B. Past event: (1) The Kāleya demons ate at night the ascetics living in the आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha (वसिष्ठस्याश्रमे विप्रा भक्षितास् तैर् दुरात्मभिः) 3. 100. 3; (2) Vasiṣṭha wanted to end his life when his sons, Śakti and the rest, were killed; when he failed to drown himself in the ocean, dejected, he returned to his आश्रम 1. 166. 45.

Vasiṣṭhasya āśramaḥ5 m.: The आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha. A. Location: On the mountain Arbuda, the son of Himavant (हिमवत्सुतम् अर्बु-दम् । … तत्राश्रमो वसिष्ठस्य) 3. 80. 74-75. B. Holiness: By living there for one night one got the reward of gifting a thousand cows (तत्रोष्य रजनीम् एकां गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्) 3. 80. 75.
Vasiṣṭhasya āśramāḥ6 m.: The आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha. Situated near the Badarīpācana tīrtha (बदरीपाचनं गच्छेद् वसिष्ठस्याश्रमं प्रति) 3. 81. 156. [See Badarapācana Vol. 1. 393]
वसिष्ठापवाह: Vasiṣṭhāpavāha m.: Name of a तीर्थ, described as a ह्रद 9. 42. 9. A. Location: On the river Sarasvatī, near Sthāṇutīrtha 9. 41. 6-7. B. Descrip-tion: Famous in the world (लोके ख्यातः) 9. 41. 39; excellent (तीर्थवर), bright (शुभ्र) 9. 42. 1; having fearful, very fearful current (भीमवेग) 9. 41. 1; (महाभीमवेग) 9. 40. 35. C. Name explained: As asked by Viśvāmitra, Sarasvatī, in order to carry off Vasiṣṭha to Viśvāmitra, removed a part of her bank on the eastern side near the आश्रम of Vasiṣṭha so that he was carried away by the water of the river Sarasvatī to the oppo-site bank near the आश्रम of Viśvāmitra; the river then carried Vasiṣṭha back (अप-वह्-) to his eastern bank; hence the तीर्थ was so called (अपोवाह वसिष्ठं तु प्राचीं दिशम् अतन्द्रिता 9. 41. 34) 9. 41. 1-39. D. Epic event: Balarāma visited it in his तीर्थयात्रा 9. 40. 35; he bathed there (उप-स्पृश्य) and gave many kinds of gifts; he thereby got religious merit (अवाप्य धर्-मम्); from there he went to Somatīrtha 9. 42. 38. E. Past event: Due to the curse of Viśvāmitra, Sarasvatī flew with blood at this तीर्थ which was drunk by the Rākṣasas; the river was later freed by as-cetics from the curse and the water near the lake became normal (प्रकृतिष्था सरस्वती । प्रसन्नसलिला जज्ञे) 9. 42. 1-13.
वसोर्: Vasor dhārā1 f.: Name of a तीर्थ। One reaches there from the Dṛmī तीर्थ (3. 80. 90-91); described as praised (by pilgrims) (अभिष्टुता) 3. 80. 92; just by visiting it one gets the fruit of a horse sacri-fice (गमनाद् एव तस्यां हि हयमेधम् अवाप्नुयात्) 3. 80. 92; a pious minded person (प्रयतात्मा), if he bathes there and gives offerings to gods and manes he is glorified in the Viṣṇuloka (विष्णुलोके महीयते) 3. 80. 93.

Vasor dhārā2 f.: Name of a heavenly river. It flows from a place where the Gan-dharvas and the Apsarases live and where there are golden palaces (प्रासादा यत्र सौवर्णाः … गन्धर्वाप्सरसो यत्र); those who give a thousand cows as a gift go to the place where Vasor dhārā flows 13. 79. 5 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 80. 5; वसोर् धारा मन्दाकिनी). [See Mandākinī2, Mandākinī3]
वस्वोकसारा: Vasvokasārā f.: Name of one of the seven streams of Gaṅgā. The divine Tripathagā (Gaṅgā) river, after it was first established on the mountain Hiraṇyaśṛṅga, got divided into seven streams; one of them was Vasvokasārā (तत्र (i. e. हिरण्यशृङ्गे) त्रिपथगा देवी प्रथमं तु प्रतिष्ठिता । ब्राह्मलोकाद् अपक्रान्ता सप्तधा प्रतिपद्यते ॥ वस्वोकसारा … ) 6. 7. 44-45, 40; one of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83, i. e. Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 94.
वस्त्रापद: Vastrāpada nt.: Name of a sacred place. One can reach it from the river Maladā; by visiting Vastrāpada and by visiting Mahā-deva (अभिगम्य महादेवम्) one gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha 3. 80. 108.
वाका: Vākā f.: Name of a river. The forest Aṅgāraparṇa, belonging to Aṅgāraparṇa Gandharva, was situated on the banks of Gaṅgā and Vākā (अङ्गारपर्णम् इति च ख्यातं वनम् इदं मम । अनु गङ्गां च वाकां च) 1. 158. 13.
वाजिनी: Vājinī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 20, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
वापी: Vāpī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 19, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
वामनक: Vāmanaka2 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Sacred to Vāmana; one can reach it from Devatīrtha; described as famous in the three worlds (त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्); by bathing at the Viṣṇupada there and by worshipping Vāmana (अर्चयित्वा च वाम-नम्) the worshipper's soul is cleansed of all sins (सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा) and he goes to the world of Viṣṇu (विष्णुलोकम् अवाप्-नुयात्) 3. 81. 86-87.
वाराह: Vārāha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as best (उत्तम); one can reach it from Aśvinos tīrtham; so called be-cause Viṣṇu formerly stood there in the form of a boar (विष्णुर् वाराहरूपेण पूर्वं यत्र स्थितो ऽभवत्); by bathing there one gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma 3. 81. 14-15.
वारिषेण: Vāriṣeṇa1 m.: Name of a mountain. Pāṇḍu crossed it after he reached the Caitraratha; after crossing Vāriṣeṇa, he cross-ed the Himavant to reach Gandhamādana 1. 110. 43.

Vāriṣeṇa2 m.: Name of an ocean. The kings who lived on the other (eas-tern) side of the Himavant, on the mountain of the sun-rise, at the shore of the Vāriṣeṇa ocean and around Lohitya and the Kirātas brought tribute, consisting of fragrant sub-stances, exotic deer and birds, and gold collected from mountains to Yudhiṣṭhira for his Rājasūya (ये परार्धे हिमवतः सूर्-योदयगिरौ नृपाः । वारिषेणसमुद्रान्ते लोहित्यम् अभितश् च ये … ये च किराताः … ॥  … गन्धानां चैव राशयः । … दूरजान् मृगपक्षिणः । विचितं पर्वतेभ्यश् च हिरण्यम् ॥ ) 2. 48. 8-11.
वालकोटि: Vālakoṭi f.: Name of a place. On the mountain Vṛṣaprastha and near the river Bāhudā 3. 93. 4.
वास्तु: Vāstu f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 24, 13; all the rivers listed here by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
विचित्रा: Vicitrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 17, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
वितस्ता: Vitastā f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of tha Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 15, 13; A Brāh-maṇa had told in the assembly of the Kurus that the river Vitastā and other four rivers along with Sindhu as the sixth flow outside the country called the Āraṭṭas (चन्द्र-भागा वितस्ता च सिन्धुषष्ठा बहिर्गताः ॥ आरट्टा नाम ते देशाः) 8. 30. 34-36. B. Description: Described as having a garland in the form of waves (ऊर्मिमालिनी) 13. 26. 7; Vitastā and the other rivers listed by Umā are described as most holy (पुण्यतमाः) and auspicious (शिवाः) 13. 134. 22; containing waters of all the तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् युताः) 13. 134. 12; excellent and best among the rivers (सरिद्वराः) 13. 134. 14; (सरि-तां वराः) 13. 134. 19; (सरिच्छ्रेष्ठाः) 13. 134. 22; expert in the knowledge of duties of women (स्त्रीधर्मकुशलाः) 13. 134. 18; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Holiness: It is said in the Tīrthavaṃśa declared by Aṅgiras to Gautama that one who observes fast and is without attachment (निराहारो निर्ममः) if he bathes for a week in Vitastā he becomes like a मुनि (सप्ताहम् … वितस्ताम् … विगाह्य वै … मुनिवद् भवेत्) 13. 26. 7; D. Impor-tance: (1) One of the rivers who wait upon Śiva for his bath (उपस्पर्शनहेतोस् त्वा समीपस्था उपासते) 13. 134. 12; Umā honoured these rivers by requesting them to instruct her in the duties of women (स्त्री-धर्म), before she could expound them to Śiva 13. 134. 14, 21, 25, 19-20; (2) Vitastā is one of the rivers who, in bodily form (2. 9. 21), wait on Varuṇa in his Sabhā 2. 9. 19, 22; (3) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 20, 2. E. Past event: Four hundred moon-white horses having one black ear each (एकतःश्यामकर्णानाम् हया-नाम् चन्द्रवर्चसाम् 5. 117. 5) were swept away by the river Vitastā at the crossing on it (चत्वारि शतानि … । नीयमानानि संतारे हृतान्य् आसन् वितस्तया) 5. 117. 8; (these horses were originally obtained by Ṛcīka at the abode of Varuṇa and given to Gādhi as bride-price in order to marry the latter's daughter Satyavatī 5. 117. 4-6).
विदिशा: Vidiśā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers who, in bodily form (2. 9. 21), wait on Varuṇa in his Sabhā 2. 9. 18, 22; listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 27, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
विद्यातीर्थ: Vidyātīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Described as best (अनुत्तम); if one reaches it in the evening and bathes there he becomes versed in all fields of knowledge (विद्यास्) (ततः संध्यां समासाद्य विद्यातीर्थम् … । उपस्पृश्य च विद्यानां सर्वासां पारगो भवेत् ॥ ) 3. 82. 47; (this explains the name of the तीर्थ).
विनशन: Vinaśana1 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: A तीर्थ on the river Sarasvatī; a place where Sarasvatī disappear-ed in a desert land (गच्छत्य् अन्तर्हिता यत्र मरुपृष्ठे सरस्वती) 3. 80. 118; Sarasvatī entered the earth as she did not want to be known to the Niṣādas due to her dislike for them; this then is the gate of the Niṣādarāṣṭra (एतद् विनशनं नाम सरस्वत्या विशां पते ॥ द्वारं निषादराष्ट्रस्य येषां द्वेषात् सरस्वती । प्रविष्टा पृथिवीं वीर मा निषादा हि मां विदुः ॥ ) 3. 130. 3-4; she disappeared also due to her dislike for the Śūdras and the Ābhīras (शूद्राभीरान् प्रति द्वेषाद् यत्र नष्टा सरस्वती) 9. 36. 1. B. Name explained: Because Sarasvatī disappeared (नष्टा) at the place of this तीर्थ, sages named it Vinaśana (यस्मात् सा भरतश्रेष्ठ द्वेषान् नष्टा सरस्वती । तस्माद् ऋषयो नित्यं प्राहुर् विनशनेति ह) 9. 36. 2. C. Holiness: A pilgrim while visiting the तीर्थ should be controlled and take restricted food (ततो विनशनं गच्छेन् नियतो नियता-शनः) 3. 80. 118. D. Epic event: Bala-rāma proceeded to Vinaśana from Udapāna 9. 35. 53; he bathed (उपस्पृश्य) there in the river Sarasvatī and went from there to Subhūmika which was also on the bank of Sarasvatī 9. 36. 3.

Vinaśana3 nt.: Name of a sacred place (?) Situated in the cave (?) of the mountain Maināka where Aditi formerly cooked food (for gods and Brāhmaṇas) to get a son (एतद् विनशनं कुक्षौ मैनाकस्य नर-र्षभ । अदितिर् यत्र पुत्रार्थं तदन्नम् अपचत् पुरा ॥ ) 3. 135. 3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 135. 3: अन्नं ब्रह्मौदनम् । अदितिः पुत्रकामा साध्येभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्रह्मौ-दनम् अपचद् इति श्रुतेः).
विनशण: Vinaśaṇa2 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in the east; from there one reaches the river Gaṇḍakī 3. 82. 97; described as one that relieves from all sins (सर्वपाप-प्रमोचन); by visiting this तीर्थ one gets the fruit of a Vājapeya and goes to the world of Soma (सोमलोकं च गच्छति) 3. 82. 96.
विन्ध्य: Vindhya m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the seven principal mountains of the Bhārata-varṣa (सप्तैते कुलपर्वताः) 6. 10. 10; described as a great mountain; the river Payoṣṇī flows by it on which there are the आश्रमस् of great sages (एष विन्ध्यो महा-शैलः पयोष्णी च समुद्रगा । आश्रमाश् च महर्षीणाम्) 3. 58. 21; it is on the way to the Dakṣiṇāpatha 3. 58. 20-21. B. Des-cription: Big mountain (महाशैल) 3. 58. 21; excellent mountain (पर्वतोत्तम) 3. 102. 11, (नगोत्तम) 3. 101. 15; king of mountains, king of big mountains (शैलराज) 3. 102. 8; (एते पर्वतराजानः) 14. 43. 4-5; (शैलेन्द्र) 3. 102. 4, 12; (महाद्रिराज) 3. 102. 6; it has many minerals, is rich in herbs (used in medicine) and has many तीर्थस् (विन्ध्यो धातुविचित्राङ्गस् तीर्थवान् औषधान्वितः) 13. 151. 25; has Śāla trees with flowering tops on it (पुष्पिताग्रेषु शालेषु) 1. 204. 6; the Karṇikāra trees grow on the banks of the rivers on this mountain (नदीतीरेषु जातान् सा कर्णिकारान् विचिन्वती) 1. 204. 10. C. Characteristic: The Mle-cchas in hundreds and thousands who arose from a person (churned out from the right thigh of Vena) live on the Vindhya (ये चान्ये विन्ध्यनिलया म्लेच्छाः शतसहस्र-शः) 12. 59. 101-103. D. Importance: (1) Listed by Brahman among the mountains which are described as kings of mountains 14. 43. 4; (are these mountains also supposed to have the quality of रजस् (मध्यमो गुणः) ? 14. 43. 1; for Nī. see Kāṣṭha-vant); (2) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 25, 2. E. Holiness: One who is truthful and causes no injury to others, if he lives on Vindhya for six months (?) and practises austerities, he is then cleansed (of sins) in a month (विन्ध्ये संताप्य चात्मानं सत्यसंधस् त्व् अहिं-सकः । षण्मासं पदम् आस्थाय मासे-नैकेन शुध्यति) 13. 26. 46. F. Past and mythological events: (1) Nala points to Vindhya while showing to Damayantī the paths leading to the Dakṣiṇāpatha and to the Vidarbhas (एते गच्छन्ति बहवः पन्-थानो दक्षिणापथम् । … एष विन्ध्यो महा-शैलः) 3. 58. 20-22; (एष पन्था विदर्-भाणाम्) 3. 58. 22; (2) Mārkaṇḍeya saw Vindhya, among other mountains, in the belly  of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 104; (3) The demons Sunda and Upasunda took दीक्षा and went to Vindhya to practise austerities; the mountain was heated for a long time by their तपस्, so it started issuing smoke; that was a miracle (तयोस् तपःप्रभावेण दीर्घकालं प्रतापितः धूमं प्रमुमुचे विन्ध्यस् तद् अद्भुतम् इवाभवत्) 1. 201. 5-9; the two demons once went to the top of Vindhya where there was level land (विन्ध्यस्य पृष्ठे समशिलातले; Nī., Bom. Ed. 1. 212. 6, reads प्रस्थे which he explains as शिखरे); Tilottamā approached the two demons there; in the duel that followed between the two over Tilottamā, both were killed on the moun-tain 1. 204. 6, 10, 19; (4) The mountain Vindhya, angry with the sun, began to grow upwards, but, at the instance of the sage Aga-stya, stopped growing (वचस् तवानतिक्रा-मन् विन्ध्यः शैलो न वर्धते) 3. 101. 15; Yudhiṣṭhira asked Lomaśa why Vindhya suddenly started to grow 3. 102. 1; Vindhya asked the sun to make a प्रदक्षिणा round him as it did round Meru; the sun told the mountain that he did not do it at his own will, but that was the course laid down by the Creator; when the sun did not oblige, Vindhya, angered, began to grow and obstructed the path of the sun and the moon; the gods tried to stop him from growing but Vindhya did not stop; the gods then approached Agastya and told him that Vindhya, under the influence of anger, was covering the path of the luminaries; they added that no one else except the sage was able to dissuade the mountain; hearing that Agastya, in the company of his wife, appro-ached Vindhya and told him that he wanted to go to the south on some purpose; he asked the mountain to wait for his return and grow again as desired after he returned; Agastya made this contract with Vindhya but never re-turned from the south; Vindhya was thus made to stop growing due to the power of Agastya (एवं स समयं कृत्वा विन्ध्येनामित्र-कर्शन । अद्यापि दक्षिणाद् देशाद् वारुणिर् न निवर्तते ॥ एतत् ते सर्वम् आख्यातं यथा विन्ध्यो न वर्धते । अगस्त्यस्य प्रभा-वेन (सिच्)) 3. 102. 3-14; (5) Vindhya, along with other mountains, arrived for the अभिषेक of Kumāra (Skanda) 9. 44. 13, 16; Vindhya presented his two companions Ucchrita and Atiśṛṅga, who fought with big rocks, to Skanda (महापाषाणयोधिनौ । प्रददाव् अग्निपुत्राय विन्ध्यः पारिषदाव् उभौ) 9. 44. 45. G. Similes: (1) Yudhiṣṭhira compared his four fallen brothers with the mountains Himavant, Pāriyātra, Vindhya and Malaya (चत्वारः पर्वताः केन पातिताः) 3. 297. 14; (2) The गदा hurled by Śrutā-yudha at Kṛṣṇa did not shake him as wind does not shake Vindhya (विन्ध्यं गिर्त्म् इवानिलः) 7. 67. 52; (3) Hanūmant as-sumed a form wonderful and very frightful, like that of Vindhya or Mandara (तद् अद्-भुतं महारौद्रं विन्ध्यमन्दरसं-निभम्) 3. 149. 10; (4) Ghaṭotkaca, afraid of Karṇa's शक्ति, ran away after as-suming a form like that of the foot of Vindhya (कृत्वात्मानं विन्ध्यपादप्रमाणम्) 7. 154. 55; (5) Yudhiṣṭhira, accompanied by the Devadūta, went along the path that was covered with corpses which were comparable to the Vindhya mountain (प्रेतैर् विन्ध्य-शैलोपमैर् वृतम्) 18. 2. 20; (6) Prati-vindhya, Yudhiṣṭhira's son, was to be another Vindhya in not taking cognisance of the hittings by opponents (परप्रहरणज्ञाने प्रतिविन्ध्यो भवत्व् अयम्) 1. 213. 74 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 221. 81: परप्रह-रणज्ञाने शत्रुकृतप्रहारवेदनायां विन्-ध्य इव निर्विज्ञान इति प्रतिविन्ध्यः).
विपापा: Vipāpā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 14, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
विपाशा: Vipāśā f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 14, 13; according to a Brāhmaṇa living in the court of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, the rivers Śatadru, Vipāśā, Irāvatī, Candrabhāgā and Vitastā, with Sindhu as the sixth, flow outside the Āraṭṭa country (पञ्च नद्यो वहन्त्य् एताः … शतद्रुश् च विपाशा च … सिन्धुषष्ठा बहिर्गताः ॥ आरट्टा नाम ते देशाः) 8. 30. 35-36; the Bāhlīka country lies between these rivers (पञ्चानां सिन्धुषष्ठानां नदीनां ये ऽन्तराश्रिताः । तान् … बाह्लीकान् परिवर्जयेत्) 8. 30. 11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 8. 44. 7: पञ्चानाम् वक्ष्य-माणानां सिन्धुः षष्ठी यासाम् अन्तरम् अवकाशम् आश्रिताः); (पञ्च नद्यो वहन्त्य् एताः … आरट्टा नाम बाह्लीकाः) 8. 30. 43; the Kālikāśrama was on this river 13. 26. 22. B. Name explained: Vasiṣṭha, grieved over the death of his sons, bound himself with fetters and threw himself in a river; the river cut off his fetters and made him as before; the sage came out of waters free of the fetters (विपाश) and named the river Vipāśā (समस्थं तम् ऋषिं कृत्वा विपाशं सम-वासृजत् ॥ उत्ततार ततः पाशैर् विमुक्तः स महान् ऋषिः । विपाशेति च नामास्या नद्याश् चक्रे महान् ऋषिः ॥ ) 1. 167. 5-6; Vasiṣṭha drowned himself due to fear of Viśvāmitra (तथैवास्य (i. e. विश्वामित्रस्य) भयाद् बद्ध्वा वसिष्ठः सलिले पुरा । आत्मानं मज्जयाम् आस विपाशः पुनर् उत्थितः ॥ तदाप्रभृति पुण्या हि विपाशा-भून् महानदी । विख्याता कर्मणा तेन वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः ॥ ) 13. 3. 12-13. C. Description: Holy (पुण्या) 13. 3. 13; highly purifying (परमपावनी) 3. 130. 8; pleasing (रम्या) 3. 130. 8; famous (वि-ख्याता) 13. 3. 13; big river (महानदी) 1. 167. 4; 13. 3. 13; full of fresh water in rainy season and washing away many trees of various kinds growing on its banks (सरितं पूर्णां प्रावृत्काले नवाम्भसा । वृक्षान् बहुविधान् पार्थ वहन्ती तीरजान् बहून्) 1. 167. 2; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā); all the rivers (Vipāśā among them) whom Umā wanted to consult on स्त्रीधर्म, are described as auspicious (शिवाः), very holy (पुण्यतमाः) 13. 134. 22; excellent rivers (सरिद्वराः) 13. 134. 14, (सरितां वराः) 13. 134. 19; best among rivers (सरिच्छ्रेष्ठाः) 13. 134. 22; contain-ing waters of all तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् युताः) 13. 134. 12; conversant with the duties of women (स्त्रीधर्मकुशलाः) 13. 134. 19. D. Characteristic: Two Piśācas named Bahi and Hlīka lived near Vipāśā; the Bāhlīkas are their progeny and not the crea-tion of Prajāpati (बहिश् च नाम ह्लीकश् च विपाशायां पिशाचकौ । तयोर् अपत्यं बाह्लीका नैषा सृष्टिः प्रजापतेः) 8. 30. 44. E. Holiness: (1) One who observes chastity and who has conquered anger if he visits Kālikāśrama, bathes in Vipāśā and stays there for three nights he is not required to return to this world again (विपाशायां कृतोदकः । ब्रह्मचारी जितक्रोधस् त्रिरात्रान् मुच्यते भवात्) 13. 26. 22; (2) Vipāśā is men-tioned among those holy places by visiting which the high-souled ones assume heavenly form and becoming auspicious and wearing heavenly garlands, rich in holy fragrance, they reach the Goloka (? ते तत्र मोदन्ति गवां विमाने 13. 105. 44) 13. 105. 46. F. Importance: (1) Vipāśā is one of the rivers who wait upon Śiva for his bath 13. 134. 12; Umā consulted them on the स्त्रीधर्म and thereby honoured them 13. 134. 14, 19-21; but Gaṅgā on behalf of all the rivers requested Umā to teach स्त्रीधर्म to them 13. 134. 29; (2) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa narrated by Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣṭhira 13. 151. 14, 2. G. Epic event: It was shown by Lomaśa to Yudhi-ṣṭhira 3. 130. 8. H. Past events: (1) Vasiṣṭha, out of grief for the death of his sons, threw himself in Vipāśā 1. 166. 39; 1. 167. 1-4; 3. 130. 9; 13. 3. 12 (see above B. Name explained); (2) Vipāśā was one of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 94.
विमल: Vimala1 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One can reach it after visiting the Giri-muñja mountain; described as the best तीर्थ (विमलं तीर्थम् उत्तमम्); it is chara-cterized by gold-coloured and silver-coloured fishes (अद्यापि यत्र दृश्यन्ते मत्स्याः सौ-वर्णराजताः); by bathing there one gets the fruit of a Vājapeya and, with his soul cleans-ed of all sins, he attains the highest state (गच्छेच् च परमां गतिम्) 3. 80. 102-104. [Identical with Vimala2 ?]

Vimala2 nt.: Name of a lake, Situated near the place which is sacred to Viśveśvara (Śiva) (तच् च विश्वेश्वर-स्थानं यत्र तद् विमलं सरः); men-tioned in the Daivata Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa narrated by Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣṭhira 13. 151. 18, 2. [Identi-cal with Vimala1 ?]
विमलाशोक: Vimalāśoka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By visiting this तीर्थ one shines like the moon (विराजति यथा शशी); by staying there for a night one is glorified in heaven (स्वर्गलोके महीयते) 3. 82. 62.
विमलोदका: Vimalodakā, Vimalodā f.: Name of one of the seven forms of Sarasvatī. Described as blessed (विमलोदा भग-वती) 9. 37. 26; when Sarasvatī was invited to appear for the sacrifices at various places by powerful persons, it appeared at those places under seven different names, one of them being Vimalodakā (आहुता बलवद्भिर् हि तत्र तत्र सरस्वती । … सुवेणुर् विमलो-दका) 9. 37. 3-4; one of the persons to invite Sarasvatī was Dakṣa; when he performed a sacrifice at the Gaṅgādvāra, Sarasvatī appear-ed there under the name Vimalodā 9. 37. 26.
विमोचन: Vimocana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By bathing (उपस्पृश्य) at this तीर्थ, one who has subdued anger and has controlled senses (जितमन्युर् जितेन्द्रियः) is freed of all faults committed in receiving gifts (प्रति-ग्रहकृतैर् दोषैः सर्वैः स परिमुच्यते) 3. 81. 140; (this explains the name).
विरज: Viraja nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated on the river Vaitaraṇī; by visiting it (विरजं तीर्थम् आसाद्य) one shines like the moon (विराजति यथा शशी), destroys all sin and is born in a holy family (प्रभवेच् च कुले पुण्ये सर्वपापं व्य-पोहति); he also gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows and purifies his family 3. 83. 6-7.
विशल्या: Viśalyā f.: Name of a river. One of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārā-yaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 95; finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa narrated by Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣṭhira 13. 151. 15.
विशाखयूप: Viśākhayūpa m.: Name of a sacred place. A. Location: In the north (उदीच्याम्) 3. 88. 1; on the Yāmuna mountain 3. 174. 15. B. Description: Most holy (पुण्यतम) 3. 88. 12. C. Epic event: The Pāṇḍavas lived in a big forest near the Viśākhayūpa for a year 3. 174. 16-17. D. Mythological event: Formerly, gods led by Indra and Varuṇa practised austerities there; hence it is holy (देवाः … अतप्यन्त तस्मात् पुण्यतमोः स वै) 3. 88. 12; all the gods had piled their sacrificial altars at Viśākhayūpa (विशाख-यूपे देवानां सर्वेषाम् अग्नयश् चिताः) 12. 12. 3 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 12. 3: वि-शाखयूपे क्षेत्रविशेषे । देवानां देवैः अग्नयो ऽग्निस्थापनार्थानि स्थंडिलानि । चिता इष्टकाभी राचिता अद्यापि दृश्यन्ते । ).
विशाला: Viśālā f.: Name of a river (or two rivers ?). A. Location: The river has its origin on the slope of the Himavant (सरित् सा हिम-वत्पार्श्वात् प्रसूता) 9. 37. 20. B. Des-cription: Famous in the three worlds (त्रै-लोक्यविश्रुता) 3. 82. 100; flowing swiftly (शीघ्रगामिनी) 9. 37. 20. C. Origin: One of the seven forms of the river Sarasvatī which pervade the whole world (राजन् सप्त सरस्वत्यो याभिर् व्याप्तम् इदं जगत्) 9. 37. 3; (seven forms of Sarasvatī are listed in 9. 37. 4); when Gaya performed a great sacrifice at Gayā (गयेषु), Sarasvatī was invited to appear there by sages; when the river appeared the sages called it Viśālā 9. 37. 19-20. D. Holiness: (1) By visiting Viśālā one gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma and goes to heaven 3. 82. 100; (2) According to the Tīrthavaṃśa narrated by Aṅgiras to Gautama one who bathes in Viśālā is absorbed in Brahman (विशालायां कृतोदकः … ब्रह्म-भूतो विराजते) 13. 26. 41; (3) According to Angiras again one who bathes in Viśālā and observes fast for twelve days is freed of all blemish (विशालायां कृतोदकः । द्वाद-शाहं निराहारः कल्मषाद् विप्रमुच्यते) 13. 26. 44; (this Viśālā may be different from the one mentioned by Aṅgiras before).
विश्वामित्रनदी: Viśvāmitranadī f.: The river Pārā so called. See Kauśikī and Pārā2 in Additions.
विश्वामित्रस्य: Viśvāmitrasya tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the Agnitīrtha (अग्नितीर्थं ततो गच्छेत् … विश्वामित्रस्य तत्रैव तीर्थम्) 3. 81. 119-120; one who bathes there is born as a Brāhmaṇa (तत्र स्नात्वा महाराज ब्राह्मण्यम् अभिजायते) 3. 81. 120.
विश्वामित्रा: Viśvāmitrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 25, 13; all rivers listed by Saṃjaya are called mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
विश्वेश्वरस्थान: Viśveśvarasthāna nt.: Name of a holy place. A dirt-free lake near the place sacred to Viśveśvara (Śiva) (तच् च विश्वेश्वरस्था-नं यत्र तद् विमलं सरः) 13. 151. 18; finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 2.
विष्णुपद: Viṣṇupada1 nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: In the north (उत्तरां दिशम् आश्रितम्) 5. 109. 19; (अस्यां दिशि … उत्तरायाम्) 5. 109. 3; situated near the Vāmanaka तीर्थ 3. 81. 86-87. B. Origin: Viṣṇu, while traversing the three worlds esta-blished it in the north (अत्र विष्णुपदं नाम क्रमता विष्णुना कृतम् । त्रिलोकवि-क्रमे) 5. 109. 19. C. Description: Ex-cellent (तीर्थम् उत्तमम्) 3. 130. 8. D. Holiness: By bathing at Viṣṇupada and by worshipping Vāmana there one is freed of sins and goes to the world of Viṣṇu 3. 81. 87.

Viṣṇupada2 m.: Name of a mountain. When King Aṅga performed a sacrifice on the Viṣṇupada mountain (विष्णुपदे गिरौ), Indra was gladdened by Soma and Brāhmaṇas by the दक्षिणास् they received (अमाद्यद् इन्द्रः सोमेन दक्षिणाभिर् द्विजातयः) 12. 29. 31.
विष्णोः: Viṣṇoḥ sthānam nt.: Name of a sacred place. Descrihed as best (अनुत्तम) 3. 81. 8; god Hari is always present there; by bathing there and by worshipping Hari one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice and goes to the world of Viṣṇu 3. 81. 8-9.
वीरप्रमोक्ष: Vīrapramokṣa nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। By visiting this तीर्थ one is freed of all sins 3. 82. 45.
वीरवती: Vīravatī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 24, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā).
वीरा: Vīrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 21, 13 (for other details see Vīravatī).
वीरिणी: Vīriṇī f.: Name of a river. A certain fish approached the bank of the river Vīriṇī and requested Manu, who was practising austerities, to save it from stronger fish; Manu took it out of the river water and put it in a small water-jar 3. 185. 6-7, 10-11.
वृद्धकन्यायास्: *Vṛddhakanyāyās tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Description: Famous (ख्यातं), large (महत्) 9. 50. 51. B. Holiness: According to a blessing given by Vṛddha-kanyā one who is composed (समाहितः) if he passes one night near the तीर्थ and satisfies gods with oblations (तर्पयित्वा दिव्-औकसः) he will get the fruit of one who has observed properly chastity for sixty-four years (चत्वारिंशतम् अष्टौ च द्वे चाष्टौ सम्-यग् आचरेत् । यो ब्रह्मचर्यं वर्षाणि फलं तस्य लभेत सः) 9. 51. 20-21. C. Past event: Kuṇī Gārgya mentally created a daughter (मानसीम् स सुतां सुभ्रूं समुत्पादितवान् विभुः); as no one was ready to marry her she started practising austerities; ultimately Śṛṅgavant Gālava married her agreeing to stay with her only for a night; next morning she reminded her husband of his agreement and, before leaving him, she blessed the place where she spent the night with him and made it a तीर्थ 9. 51. 3-20.
वृषदंश: Vṛṣadaṃśa m.: Name of a mountain. Described as chief among the mountains (शैलेन्द्र) 7. 57. 29; one of the mountains seen by Arjuna when he journeyed through space towards the north (7. 57. 23) on his way to propitiate Śiva for his Pāśupata missile 7. 57. 16-17, 29.
वृषप्रस्थ: Vṛṣaprastha m.: Name of a mountain. Situated in Vālakoṭī; the Pāṇḍavas lived there before they took bath in the river Bāhuda (वालकोट्यां वृषप्रस्थे गिराव् उष्य च पाण्डवाः) 3. 93. 4.
वृषभ: Vṛṣabha m.: Name of a mountain. One of the five mountains surrounding Girivraja in the Magadha; by coming close to one another they as if protected Girivraja (रक्षन्तीवाभिसंहत्य संहताङ्गा गिरि-व्रजम्) 2. 19. 2-3; all the five mountains are described as having high peaks (महा-शृङ्गाः), cool trees (शीतलद्रुमाः) 2. 19. 3; the mountains were covered by forests of Lodhra trees which were fragrant, attractive, and their branches full of flowers; they were liked by lovers 2. 19. 4.
वृषभङ्गिनी: Vṛṣabhaṅginī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 34, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
वृषभा: Vṛṣabhā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 31, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
वेण्णा: Veṇṇā f.: Name of a river. A. Location: In the south (दक्षिण-स्याम्) 3. 86. 1; listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 26, 13. B. Des-cription: Having holy water (पुण्यतोया); bringing what is auspicious to the visitor (शुभावहा) 3. 186. 95; removing fear of sin (पापभयापहा) 3. 86. 3; thronged by deer and birds (मृगद्विजसमाकीर्णा) and adorned by the hermitages of ascetics (ताप-सालयभूषिता) 3. 86. 3; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Holiness: (1) By satisfying manes and gods at Veṇṇā one rides in a Vimāna that is drawn by peacocks and swans (तर्पयेत् पितृदेवताः । मयूर-हंससंयुक्तं विमानं लभते नरः) 3. 83. 29; (2) By bathing at the confluence of Veṇṇā (वेण्णायाः संगमे स्नात्वा) one gets the fruit of a Vājapeya 3. 83. 31. D. Past event: One of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 95. E. Importance: (1) Listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among the rivers which are declared to be mothers of fire-hearths (i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed) 3. 212. 23-24 (for citation and Nī. see Kapilā); (2) finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 17, 2.
वेतसिका: Vetasikā f.: Name of a river. Inhabited by Pitāmaha (Brahman) (पितामहनिषेविता); one who visits it (गत्वा) gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and the world of Uśanas (गच्छेच् चौशनसीं गतिम्) 3. 82. 50 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 3. 84. 56: औशनसीं गतिं शुक्रत्वम्).
वेतसिनी: Vetasinī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 16, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
वेत्रवती: Vetravatī f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya twice among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 15, 18, 13 (or in 6. 10. 18 वेत्रवती is Carmaṇvatī's epithet ‘full of reeds’). B. Description: All the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong (विश्वस्य मातरः सर्वाः सर्वाश् चैव महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35. C. Past event: One of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 93. D. Importance: (1) Listed by Mārkaṇḍeya among rivers which are proclaimed to be mothers of fire-hearths, i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed 3. 212. 22 (for citation and Nī. see Kapilā); (2) Finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 16, 2.
वेदस्मृति: Vedasmṛti f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 16, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā); finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 20, 2.
वेदाश्वा: Vedāśvā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 27, 13 (for other details see Atikṛṣṇā).
वेदी: Vedī1 f.: Name of a sacred place. Described as highly inaccessible (परम-दुर्गमा) 3. 82. 42; by visiting it one gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and obtains the condition of Uśanas (गच्छेच् चौशनसीं गतिम्) 3. 82. 42 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 3. 84. 56: औशनसीं गतिं शुक्रत्वम्)

Vedī2 f.: Name of a sacred place having the form of an altar. A. Origin: Viśvakarman offered a sacrifice in the forest of Svayaṃbhū (Brah-man); at this sacrifice Svayaṃbhū gave the entire earth as दक्षिणा to Kaśyapa; angered at being gifted to a mortal, the earth entered Rasātala; when propitiated by Kaśyapa, the earth emerged from water and appeared in the form of an altar (पुनर् उन्मज्ज्य सलिताद् वेदीरूपा स्थिता बभौ ॥ सैषा प्रकाशते राजन् वेदीसंस्थानलक्षणा) 3. 114. 17-23. B. Characteristic: If touched by a mortal the Vedī would enter the ocean (स्पृष्टा हि मर्त्येन ततः समुद्रम् एषा वेदी प्रविशति  … ) 3. 114. 24; hence described as ‘going to the ocean’ (सागरगा) 3. 114. 26. C. Holiness: By ascending it one is endowed with virility (आरुह्यात्र महाराज वीर्यवान् वै भविष्यसि) 3. 114. 23. D. Epic event: As advised by Lomaśa, Yudhiṣṭhira ascended the Vedī; before he did it, Lomaśa pronounced on him benediction (स्वस्त्ययन); Yudhi-ṣṭhira was also to utter the following truth (सत्यवाक्य) while ascending the altar; अग्निर् मित्रो योनिर् आपो ऽथ देव्यो विष्णो रेतस् त्वम् अमृतस्य नाभिः 3. 114. 24-26.
वेद्या: Vedyā f.: Name of a river. Described as having water for most part of the year (? बहुशोजला) 13. 26. 41; by bathing there (उपस्पृश्य) a person becomes one with Brahman (ब्रह्मभूतो विराजते) 13. 26. 41.
वैजयन्त: Vaijayanta m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: In the midst of the ocean of milk (क्षीरोदस्य समुद्रस्य मध्ये) 12. 338. 9. B. Description: Well known (ख्यात) 12. 333. 9; excellent mountain (पर्वतप्रवर) 12. 338. 9, (गिरिवर) 12. 338. 21; having lustre like that of gold (हाटकसमप्रभ) 12. 338. 9; where god Brahman walks (त्वत् (i. e. Brahman) पाद-सेवित) 12. 338. 17. C. Characteristic: God Brahman abandons his own residence (12. 338. 19-20) and takes his resort on this mountain to meditate with great concentration on Virāj Puruṣa (वैजयन्तो गिरिवरः सत-तं सेव्यते मया । अत्रैकाग्रेण मनसा पुरुषश् चिन्त्यते विराट्) 12. 338. 21. D. Mythological event: On this mountain god Brahman, sitting all alone in his residence, meditates constantly on the nature of the Supreme Soul (तत्राध्यात्मगतिं देवः एकाकी प्रविचिन्तयन् । वैराजसदने नित्यं वैजयन्तं निषेवते ॥ ) 12. 338. 10; once, while he was sitting on the mountain, Śiva, his son born to him from his forehead, happened to go there travelling through space; a dialogue between the two took place on this mountain on the nature of the great, eternal Puruṣa 12. 338. 11-25; 12. 339. 1-21.
वैडूर्यपर्वत: Vaiḍūryaparvata, Vaiḍūryaśikhara m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: In the south (दक्षिण-स्याम् 3. 86. 1) 3. 86. 15, and in the west, in the Avanti, country (अवन्तिषु प्रतीच्यां वै … दिशि) 3. 87. 1; the river Narmadā flows by it 3. 121. 15; the mountain can be reached from the river Payoṣṇī 3. 121. 15. B. Des-cription: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 87. 4, 6; auspi-cious (शिव) 3. 86. 15; 3. 87. 4; excellent mountain (गिरिवर) 3. 87. 4; illustrious (श्रीमन्त्) 3. 86. 15; full of jewels (मणि-मय) 3. 86. 15; heavenly (दिव्य), com-parable with heaven (स्वर्गोपम) 3. 87. 6; always resorted to by gods and sages (नित्यं देवर्षिसेवितः) 3. 87. 6; meeting place of the river Narmadā and the Vaiḍūrya mountain is described as the meeting place of the Tretā and the Dvāpara Yugas (सन्धिर् एष नर-श्रेष्ठ त्रेताया द्वापरस्य च) 3. 121. 18-19. C. Characteristic: (1) On the peak of this mountain is a lake of Dhīmant (?) (तस्य शैलस्य शिखरे सरस् तत्र च धी-मतः) which has full blown lotuses and which is visited by gods and Gandharvas 3. 87. 5; (2) Trees on this mountain have hea-venly flowers and fruits and they are always green (दिव्यपुष्पफलास् तत्र पादपा हरि-तच्छदाः) 3. 87. 4; (3) There are many wonderful things on this mountain (बह्व्-आश्चर्यं महाराज दृश्यते तत्र पर्वते) 3. 87. 6. D. Holiness: By seeing (दृष्ट्वा) the Vaiḍūrya mountain one goes to the world of gods and (righteous) kings (देवानाम् एति कौन्तेय तथा राज्ञां सलोकताम्) 3. 121. 18; by visiting the meeting place of Vaiḍūrya and Narmadā one is freed of all sins 3. 121. 19. E. Epic event: Yudhiṣṭhira and his brothers reached the mountain after bathing in Payoṣṇī 3. 121. 15.
वैतरणी: Vaitaraṇī1 f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 33, 13; in the Kaliṅga country (एते कलिङ्गाः कौन्तेय यत्र वैतरणी नदी) 3. 114. 4; flowing near the तीर्थ Triviṣṭapa 3. 81. 70 and the तीर्थ Viraja 3. 83. 6. B. Description: Holy (पुण्या) 3. 81. 70; releasing from sins (पापप्रमोचनी) 3. 81. 70; 3. 83. 6; the northern bank of Vaitaraṇī is described as adorned by a moun-tain; this bank is fit for performing sacrifices, is thronged by sages and is always visited by Brāhmaṇas (ऋषिभिः समुपायुक्तं यज्ञियं गिरिशोभितम् । उत्तरं तीरम् एतद् धि सत-तं द्विजसेवितम् ॥ ) 3. 114. 5; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Holiness: (1) By bathing in Vaitaraṇī and by wor-shipping there god Vṛṣadhvaja (Śiva) one is cleansed of all sins and he obtains the highest condition (गच्छेत परमां गतिम्) 3. 81. 71; (2) By visiting Vaitaraṇī (and also the तीर्थ Viraja) one shines like moon (विराजति यथा शशी); he destroys all sins and, (after death), is born in a meritorious family (प्रभवेच् च कुले पुण्ये); he gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows and purifies his family 3. 83. 6-7; (3) Its northern bank specially suitable for performing sacrifices (यज्ञियं … उत्तरं तीरम्) 3. 114. 5 (see the section on Past and mythological events); (4) One who touches the water of this river and recites the following गाथा (called Anuvaṃśa of Rudra): अयातयामं सर्वेभ्यो भागेभ्यो भागम् उत्तमम् । देवाः संकल्पयाम् आसुर् भयाद् रुद्रस्य शाश्वतम् (3. 114. 11) goes (to heaven) by the देवयान and his eye shines (इमां गाथाम् अत्र गायन्न् अपः स्पृशति यो नरः । देवयानस् तस्य पन्थाश् चक्षुश् चैव प्रकाशते) 3. 114. 12. D. Epic events: Pointed out by Lomaśa to Yudhiṣṭhira 3. 114. 4; the Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī descended into the river Vaitaraṇī and gave offerings to manes (अवतीर्य महाभागा (? महाभागां) तर्पयां चक्रिरे पितॄन्) 3. 114. 13; Yudhi-ṣṭhira told Lomaśa that by bathing (उप-स्पृश्य) in the river he went above the realm of human beings and saw all the worlds and (heard) the sound of the Vaikhānasas who were offering prayers (मानुषाद् अस्मि विषयाद् अपेतः पश्य लोमश । सर्वाल्̃ लोकान् प्रपश्यामि … वैखानसानाम् जपताम् एष शब्दो महात्मनाम्) 3. 114. 14-15; Lomaśa then told him that the sound he was hearing was coming from a distance of three hundred thousand योजनस् and that he should keep quiet (तूष्णीम् आस्स्व विशां पते) 3. 114. 16. E. Past and mythological events: (1) Sages formerly offered sacrifices on the bank of Vaitaraṇī and went to heaven by a path similar to the देवयान (समेन देव-यानेन पथा स्वर्गम् उपेयुषः । अत्र वै ऋषयो ऽन्ये ऽपि पुरा क्रतुभिर् ईजिरे) 3. 114. 6; (2) Here Dharma himself took refuge with gods and offered a sacrifice (यत्रायजत धर्मो ऽपि देवाञ् शरणम् एत्य वै) 3. 114. 4; (3) Here Rudra once took away the sacrificial animal (पशु) in a sacrifice saying ‘this is (my) share’; gods then requested him not to take away what belonged to some one else and destroy the धर्मस्; they praised Rudra and satisfied him with a sacrifice and honoured him; Rudra then let go the sacrificial animal and went away by the Devayāna 3. 114. 7-10; (4) Near the river Vaitaraṇī was the wood of Svayaṃbhū where Viśvakarman offered a sacrifice 3. 114. 17 (for details see Vedī2).

Vaitaraṇī2 f.: Name of a river. Situated in the south 5. 107. 1; it was sought by those who wished to go beyond (the cycle of life and death) (अत्र वैतरणी नाम नदी वितरणैर् वृता) (this explains the name of the river); by reaching it one puts an end both to happiness and misery (अत्र गत्वा सुखस्यान्तं दुःखस्यान्तं प्रपद्यते) 5. 107. 14 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 5. 109. 14-15: वितरणैः वैत-रणीनदीसज्ञकनरकगामिभिः । सुख-स्यान्तं नरकं दुःखस्यान्तं स्वर्ग-सुखम्).

Vaitaraṇī3 f.: Name of a mythological river; also called Mahāvaitaraṇī (6. 55. 125; 8. 58. 7; 8. 68. 18) A. Location: In the realm of Yama (वैतरण्यां … यमक्षये) 12. 290. 31; flows towards the kingdom of Yama (यथा वैतरणी राजन् यमराष्ट्रपुरं प्रति) 7. 146. 47; 6. 99. 38. B. Description: Big river (महानदी) 12. 309. 31; hot (उष्णा) 12. 309. 31; cruel (क्रूरा) 6. 55. 125; fierce (उग्रा) 8. 55. 42; frightful (घोरा) 16. 6. 10; very frightful (सुघोरा) 6. 55. 121; (सुभीमा) 6. 55. 125; (महाभया) 7. 48. 50; painful to look at (दुर्दृशा) 8. 68. 18; river of blood (असृग्जला) 7. 48. 49; (शोणि-तौघतरङ्गिणी) 7. 146. 47; difficult to cross (दुस्तरा) 7. 48. 50; difficult to cross by evildoers (दुस्तरा पापकर्मभिः) 1. 158. 19; difficult to cross by those who have not realized the Soul (वैतरणीम् … दुस्तराम् अकृतात्मभिः) 8. 55. 42 (also see section F. Similes below). C. Characteristic: A person who does evil deeds (दुष्कृतकर्मा 12. 309. 30) plunges into Vaitaraṇī; his limbs are cut by a forest of sword-sharp leaves and, lying on the bed of axes, he lives in hell, severely afflicted 12. 309. 31; those who fall in Vaitaraṇī experience grief (वैत-रण्यां च यद् दुःखं पतितानाम्) 12. 290. 31; (knowing it the followers of the Sāṃkhya doctrine seek knowledge and go beyond the phenomenon of birth 12. 290. 69). D. Form of Gaṅgā: Dvaipāyana (Vyāsa) had declared that the river Gaṅgā became Vaitaraṇī after reaching the world of Pitṛs and was difficult to cross by evildoers (तथा पितॄन् वैतरणी दुस्तरा पापकर्मभिः । गङ्गा भवति गन्धर्व यथा द्वैपायनो ऽब्रवीत् ॥ ) 1. 158. 19. E. Epic event: When Indra and other gods and Dharma in bodily form came to meet Yudhiṣṭhira, the river Vaitaraṇī with its thorny Śālmali trees disappeared (नदी वैतरणी चैव कूट-शाल्मलिना सह (नादृश्यत)) 18. 3. 1-2, 4-5. F. Similes: (1) The river of blood of the warriors killed by Arjuna (6. 55. 121) compared with Mahāvaitaraṇī (महावैत-रणीप्रकाशाम्) 6. 55. 125; (2) The river of blood and entrails (लोहितान्त्रतरङ्गिणी) flowing on the field of battle and carrying away the timid ones compared with Vaitaraṇī which carries corpses to the city of Yama (यथा वैतरणी प्रेतान् प्रेतराजपुरं प्रति) 6. 99. 38; (3) The river made to flow on the field of battle by prominent warriors (योधवरैः प्रवर्तिता रणनदी) com-pared to Vaitaraṇī 7. 48. 50; (4) The river of blood with mud (शोणितकर्दमाम् ॥ शोणि-तोदाम्) made to flow by Bhīma compared with Vaitaraṇī 8. 55. 38-39, 42; (5) The battle-field appeared like Mahāvaitaraṇī (रणभूमिर् अभूद् राजन् महावैतरणी यथा) 8. 58. 7; (6) Dvārakā, bereft of Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa and other Yādava heroes, appeared as frightful to Arjuna as Vaitaraṇī (घोरां नदीं वैतरणीम् इव) 16. 6. 10.
वैतसिका: Vaitasikā f.: Name of a river. Described as one that is resorted to by Pitāmaha (Brahman); by reaching it one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice and obtains the condition of Uśanas (Śukra) (पितामह-निषेविताम् । अश्वमेधम् अवाप्नोति गच्छेच् चौशनासीं गतिम्) 3. 82. 50 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 84. 56: औशनसीम् गतिं शुक्रत्वम्).
वैदसिनी: Vaidasinī f.: Name of a river. Mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 20, 2.
वैनन्दी: Vainandī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 26, 13; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā).
वैमानिक: Vaimānika nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the Kiṅkiṇīkāśrama; according to the Tīrthavaṃśa narrated by Aṅgiras to Gautama (13. 26. 3-4) one who bathes (उपस्पृश्य) there is able to move at will and is glorified in the heavenly abode of the Apsarases (निवासे ऽप्सरसां दिव्ये कामचारी महीयते) 13. 26. 21.
वैवस्वतस्य: Vaivasvatasya tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। According to the Tīrthavaṃśa narrated by Aṅgiras to Gautama (13. 26. 3-4) one who bathes (उपस्पृश्य) in this तीर्थ him-self becomes a तीर्थ (तीर्थभूतो भवेन् नरः) 13. 26. 37.

Vaivasvatasya āyatanam nt.: Name of a holy resort (temple ?) of Vaivasvata. A. Location: In a holy forest, not very far from the sea and the तीर्थ known as Śūrpāraka (शूर्पारकम् ददर्श ॥ तत्रो-दधेः कंचिद् अतीत्य देशम् … वनम् आससाद) 3. 118. 8-9; (स तत्र … वैवस्व-तस्य … आयतनानि तेषाम् ददर्श) 3. 118. 10-11, 13. For B. Description and C. Epic event see Bhagasya āyatanam.
वैहायस: Vaihāyasa m.: Name of a lake (called ह्रद, also सरस्). Situated near the आश्रम of Naranārā-yaṇa (समासादितवान् दिव्यं नरनारायणा-श्रमम् । यत्र … ह्रदो वैहायसस् तथा) 12. 126. 2-3; sage Ṛṣabha (12. 126. 1) satis-fied gods and manes at this lake by giving offerings according to the rites and then visited the आश्रम (तस्मिन् सरसि कृत्वाहं विधिवत् तर्पणं पुरा । पितॄणाम् देवता-नां च ततोऽश्रमम् इयां तदा ॥ ) 12. 126. 2-4.
वैहार: Vaihāra m.: Name of a mountain. One of the five mountains surrounding Girivraja, the capital of the Magadha country; described as having wide extent (वैहारो विपुलः शैलः) 2. 19. 2; these five mounta-ins, coming close to one another, as if guard-ed the Girivraja (रक्षन्तीवाभिसंहत्य संहताङ्गा गिरिव्रजम्) 2. 19. 3 (for the description of the five mountains see Ṛṣigiri.
व्यासवन: Vyāsavana nt.: Name of a forest. The lake Manojava is located in this forest 3. 81. 78.

Vyāsavana nt.: A forest named after Vyāsa. One proceeds to Vyāsavana from the तीर्थ called Miśraka 3. 81. 76; while visits ing this आश्रम, one should be controlled and should take limited food (ततो व्यासव-नं गच्छेन् नियतो नियताशनः) 3. 81. 78; the तीर्थ called Manojava was in Vyāsa-vana (ततो व्यासवनं गच्छेन् … ) 3. 81. 78. [See also the next]
व्यासस्थली: Vyāsasthalī f.: Name of a sacred place. It was here that Vyāsa, afflicted by grief over the disappearance of his son (Śuka) (cf. 12. 320. 26, 32), decided to give up his body; but his spirits were again raised by gods (यत्र व्यासेन धीमता । पुत्रशोकाभितप्-तेन देहत्यागार्थनिश्चयः ॥ कृतो देवैश् च राजेन्द्र पुनर् उत्थापितस् तदा । ); by visiting the place one gets the fruit of gifting a thousand cows 3. 81. 81-82.

Vyāsasthalī f.: Name of a place. Located in Vyāsavana (ततो व्यासवनं गच्छेन् … ) 3. 81. 78; Vyāsa, grieved over the departure of his son, decided to end his life at this place; he was however, comforted by gods (ततो व्यासस्थली नाम यत्र व्या-सेन धीमता । पुत्रशोकाभितप्तेन देह-त्यागार्थनिश्चयः ॥ कृतो देवैश् च राजेन्द्र पुनर् उत्थापितस् तदा) 3. 81. 81-82 (in the Śāntiparvan it is reported that Vyāsa, griev-ed over his separation from Śuka, sat down, dejected, on the slope of HImavant; he was there comforted by Śiva who arrived with gods and Gandharvas 12. 320. 27-38); one who visits Vyāsasthalī gets the fruits of gift-ing a thousand cows (अभिगम्य स्थलीं तस्य गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्) 3. 81. 82.
व्योमगङ्गा: Vyomagaṅgā f.: Name of the heavenly Gaṅgā. After explaining to Śuka the nature of the seven winds, who are the sons of Aditi (एवम् एते ऽदितेः पुत्रा मारुताः परमा-द्भुताः) 12. 315. 36-53), and after asking him to continue his Vedic study Vyāsa left for Vyomagaṅgā (उक्त्वा पुत्रम् अधीष्वेति व्योमगङ्गाम् अयात् तदा) 12. 315. 57. [See Ākāśagaṅgā]
वरुणस्य: Varuṇasya āśramaḥ m.: See Mitrasya  … āśramaḥ.
वर्धमानद्वार: Vardhamānadvāra, Vardhamānapuradvāra  nt.: Name of the gate of Hāstina-pura facing the town Vardhamāna. Epic events: (1) Kuntī, after the death of Pāṇḍu, came in the company of the ascetics and her sons to Kurujāṅgala and from there she reached the Vardhamāna-puradvāra before entering Hāstinapura (सा … संप्राप्ता कुरुजाङ्गलम् । वर्ध-मानपुरद्वारं आससाद यशस्विनी ॥ ) 1. 117. 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 1. 10: वर्ध-मानपुरं नाम ग्रामविशेषः । तदभि-मुखं द्वारम्; however, on 1. 126. 9 he simply says: वर्धमानपुरद्वारं मुख्यद्वारम्); (2) The Pāṇḍavas when they left Hāstinapura for their exile, came out of the Vardhamānapura gate and went to the north (निर्ययुर् गजसाह्वयात् । वर्धमानपुरद्वारेणाभिनिष्क्रम्य ते त-दा । उदङ्मुखाः … प्रययुः ॥ ) 3. 1. 8-9; (3) When Dhṛtarāṣṭra decided to repair to the forest he left Hāstinapura coming out of the Vardhamānadvāra (स वर्ध-मानद्वारेण निर्ययौ गजसाह्वयात्) 15. 22. 3; (Vardhamānadvāra, according to S. K. Belvalkar, means ‘an entrance or exit other than the southern’, cf. दक्षिणाद्वारहीनं तु वर्धमानम् उदाहृतम् from the Bṛhat-saṃhitā of Varāhamihira 53. 33. 36 cited by him. Dr. Belvalkar further observes: “It is also the name of a specific gate of Hastinā-pura”, his note on the stanza in the Cr. Ed. Vol. 19, p. 153. The Bṛhatsaṃhitā passage, however, seems to mean that a house which does not have a gate to the south is called Vardhamāna. The editions of the Bṛhat-saṃhitā consulted by me read in 53. 33 as तद्वच् च (or तस्मिंश् च) वर्धमाने द्वारं तु न दक्षिणं कार्यम्).
वर्धमानपुर: Vardhamānapura nt.: Name of a town. Suburb of Hāstinapura; one of the gates of Hāstinapura faced this town; see Vardhamānadvāra.
वातिकषण्ड: Vātikaṣaṇḍa m.: Name of a place. To the north of the Videhas (विदेहान् उत्तरं च यः): described as famous and truely powerful; nobody approached its gate (एष वातिकषण्डो वै प्रख्यातः सत्य-विक्रमः । नाभ्यवर्तत यद्द्वारं विदे-हान् उत्तरं च यः ॥ ) 3. 130. 13 (However, Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 130. 13 takes वातिकषण्ड to mean ‘a collection of lotuses etc. brought by wind’: यद् वर्षस्य द्वारं एषो ऽनुभू-यमानो वातिकषण्डो वातानीतः पद्मादिस-मूहो नात्यवर्तत … । अनेन वायोर् अप्य् अस्मिन् वर्षे प्रवेशो नास्ति किमुतेतरस्येति । Nī. construes the stanza quite differently. He connects it with the वर्षम् of the preceding stanza (12) and according to him the stanza is intended to reveal the prowess of (Paraśu) Rāma.
वारणा: Vāraṇā f.: Short for Vāraṇāvata ? One of the places to which the army of the Kauravas, gathered for the war, spread out since it could not be contained in Hāstinapura (न हास्तिनपुरे राजन्न् अवकाशो ऽभवत् तदा 5. 19. 28; वारणा वाटधानं च । … एष देशः सुविस्तीर्णः  … बभूव कौरवेयाणां बलेन सुसमा-कुलः) 5. 19. 30-31.
वारणावत: Vāraṇāvata nt.: Name of a city. A. Description: Pleasing (रम्य) 1. 131. 2, 5; (रमणीय) 1. 131. 14; more pleasing than any other town (रमणीय-तरं लोके) 1. 131. 7; attractive place for men (पुंसाम् देशे मनोरमे) 1. 131. 4; full of all kinds of jewels (सर्वरत्नसमा-कीर्ण) 1. 131. 4; full of people (जनाकीर्ण) 1. 131. 14; usually referred to as नगर 1. 131. 2, 3, 5, 7, 14; 1. 132. 15, 18; 1. 134. 1; 1. 137. 12, 17; 2. 69. 12; 10. 11. 23; the people of the town called नागर (नागरं जनम्) 1. 133. 30; (नागरो जनः) 1. 137. 1; (नागराः) 1. 137. 9; (नराः नगरवासिनः) 1. 135. 21; on a few occasions referred to as पुर 1. 134. 6; people of the town called पौर 1. 134. 5, 8; पुरनिवासिन् 1. 134. 10; called ग्राम when listed among the places for which the Pāṇḍavas were ready to settle with the Kauravas 5. 31. 20; 5. 70. 14; 5. 80. 7. B. Place of festival: A famous festival in honour of god Paśupati (Śiva) used to be held at Vāraṇāvata which attracted visi-tors; it used to be the talk of the nearby towns like Hāstinapura (केचित् कुशलमन्-त्रिणः । कथयां चक्रिरे … अयं समाजः सुमहान् रमाणीयतरो भुवि । उपस्थितः पशुपतेर् नगरे वारणावते) 1. 131. 2-3, 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 143. 3: समाजः पशुपतेः पूजार्थं मेलकः). C. Epic events: (1) Duryodhana suggested to Dhṛtarāṣṭra to persuade the Pāṇḍavas to visit Vāraṇāvata and stay there for some time; they would return from there to Hāstinapura when Duryodhana felt esta-blished in the kingdom (विवासयितुम् अर्हति मृदुनैवाभ्युपायेन नगरं वारणाव-तम्) 1. 130. 10-11; there would be no fault in removing the Pāṇḍavas and their mother to Vāraṇāvata (नात्र दोषो भवि-ष्यति) 1. 130. 19; at the instance of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra his clever ministers began to praise Vāraṇāvata 1. 131. 2-5; hearing the descrip-tion of Vāraṇāvata, the Pāṇḍavas desired to go there; Dhṛtarāṣṭra permitted the Pāṇḍa-vas to go to Vāraṇāvata to see the festival and enjoy themselves there; they might give gifts to Brāhmaṇas and singers as desired and then return to Hāstinapura 1. 131. 7-10; Yudhiṣṭhira told Bhīṣma and others his wish to live in Vāraṇāvata for some days and prayed for their blessings so that no harm would come to them (आशीर्भिर् वर्-धितान् अस्मान् न पापं प्रषहिष्यति) 1. 131. 14-15; after receiving the blessings the Pāṇḍavas left for Vāraṇāvata 1. 131. 18; (2) Duryodhana told Purocana that the Pāṇḍavas were sent away to Vāraṇā-vata by Dhṛtarāṣṭra for the festival there; he asked Purocana to rush to Vāraṇāvata the same day in a chariot drawn by don-keys 1. 132. 6-7; Purocana was to build at Vāraṇāvata for the Pāṇḍavas a house of four halls, well concealed, and in the construction of which all sorts of infla-mable materials were to be used (चतुःशा-लं गृहं परमसंवृतम् । … यानि द्र-व्याणि कानिचित् । … आग्नेयान्य् उत सन्तीह तानि सर्वाणि दापय) 1. 132. 8-9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 144. 9: आग्नेयानि अग्निसंदीपकानि); Purocana was to ask the Pāṇḍavas and Kuntī to live in that house; he was to see that the Pāṇḍavas lived at Vāraṇāvata with comfort and without fear; he was later to set the house on fire 1. 132. 13, 15-16; accordingly Purocana left for Vāraṇā-vata in a chariot drawn by donkeys 1. 132. 18; (3) The Pāṇḍavas left for Vāraṇā-vata (प्रययुर् वारणावतं 1. 133. 4) on the eighth day of the month of Phalguna and under the Rohiṇī constellation; on reaching it they met the citizens of the town (अष्टमे ऽहनि रोहिण्यां प्रयाताः फल्गुनस्य ते । वारणावतम् आसाद्य ददृशुर् नागरं जनम् ॥ ) 1. 133. 30; the people of Vāraṇāvata, delighted, came out to receive the Pāṇḍavas with all auspicious things; they pronounced blessings for their victory and waited on them (वारणावतका जनाः । कृत्वा जयाशिषः सर्वे परिवार्योपतस्थिरे) 1. 134. 1-3; 5-6; The Pāṇḍavas entered the town and visited the houses of all the four classes and were led to their residence by Purocana 1. 134. 5-8; (4) The citizens of Vāraṇāvata believed that the Pāṇḍavas were burnt by fire and lamented their death 1. 136. 13-15; the Pāṇḍavas, however, had escaped with their mother from the house at Vāraṇāvata through a tunnel and went to the south 1. 136. 15. (प्रययुः … दक्षी-णां दिशम् आश्रिताः) 1. 137. 17; (दक्षिणा-मुखाः) 1. 137. 18; (5) Dhṛtarāṣṭra sent his men to Vāraṇāvata to perform the fune-ral rites of the Pāṇḍavas and Kuntī 1. 137. 12; (6) Bhīma lamented that the Pāṇḍavas could not sleep even on the best beds at Vāraṇāvata (शयनेषु परार्ध्येषु ये पुरा वारणावटे । नाधिजग्मुस् तदा निद्राम् … ) 1. 138. 15; (7) Attempt on the life of the Pāṇḍavas at Vāraṇāvata and their escape from the house of lac with the help of Bhīma referred to (i) by Kuntī while talking to Yudhiṣṭhira 1. 150. 15; (ii) by Drau-padī while talking to Kṛṣṇa 3. 13. 78; (iii) by Saṃjaya while talking to Dhṛtarāṣṭra 5. 49. 18, 20; (iv) by Kṛṣṇa while talking to Duryodhana 5. 126. 13; (v) by Bhīma while addressing Duryodhana 9. 32. 37 = 9. 55. 28; (vi) by Draupadī while talking to Bhīma 10. 11. 23; (vii) the burning of the lac house (at Vāraṇāvata) is listed in the Parvasaṃgrahaparvan (दाहो जतुगृहस्य) 1. 2. 35, and the going of the Pāṇḍavas to Vāraṇāvata is referred to in the detailed con-tents of the Ādiparvan (वारणावतयात्रा च) 1. 2. 83; (8) Vidura reminded Yudhiṣṭhira that he was formerly instructed by Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana at Vāraṇāvata (अनुशिष्टो ऽसि … । द्वैपायन कृष्णेन नगरे वाराणावते ॥ ) 2. 69. 12 (this incident is not reported in the epic account of Pāṇḍavas' stay at Vāraṇā-vata 1. 134-136); (9) The kings fighting with Yuyutsu for six months at Vāraṇāvata were not able to defeat him (यं (i. e. युयुत्-सुम्) योधयन्तो राजानो नाजयन् वारणा-वते । षण्मासान्) 7. 9. 54 (the incident is not reported in the epic); (10) Vāraṇāvata figures among the four of the five villages specifically named by Yudhiṣṭhira for which he was ready to settle with the Kauravas (कुशस्थलं वृकस्थलम् आसन्दी वारणाव-तम् ॥ भ्रातॄणाम् देहि पञ्चानाम् ग्रामान् पञ्च सुयोधन) 5. 31. 19-20; 5. 70. 15-16; 5. 80. 7.
वाराणसी: Vārāṇasī f.: Name of a town, capi-tal of Kāśi, hence referred to also as Kaśi-purī (5. 175. 17; 6. 14. 6; 13. 154. 23); Kāśinagarī (5. 174. 11). A. History: It was founded by Divo-dāsa, son of Sudeva, at the instance of Indra (दिवोदासस् तु … वाराणसीं महातेजा निर्ममे शक्रशासनात्) 13. 31. 16. B. Loca-tion: On the northern bank of Gaṅgā, behind a protective wall, and to the south of the river Gomatī (गङ्गाया उत्तरे कूले वप्रान्ते … । गोमत्या दक्षिणे चैव) 13. 31. 18 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 30. 18: वप्रान्ते तटसमीपे). C. Capital town: Place of residence of the king of Kāśi (काशिपती राजा वाराणस्याम्) 5. 49. 38. D. (1) Des-cription: Crowded with all the four classes (विप्रक्षत्रियसंबाधां वैश्यशूद्रसमा-कुलाम्) 13. 31. 17; having heaps of many kinds of goods (नैकद्रव्योच्चयवती) 13. 31. 17; having markets of prosperous shops (समृद्धविपणापणा) 13. 31. 17. (2) Called पुरी 1. 96. 4; 12. 253. 45; 13. 31. 22; 14. 6. 27, 28, 29; (काशि) पुरी 5. 175. 17; 6. 14. 6; 13. 154. 23; नगरी 5. 47. 40; 14. 6. 22; (काशि) नगरी 5. 174. 11. E. Holy place: One who worships Vṛṣadhvaja (Śiva) at Vārāṇasī gets the fruits of a राजसूय sacri-fice 3. 82. 69. F. Epic events: (1) Hearing that the three Kāśi princesses were holding a स्वयंवर, Bhīṣma, in a single chariot, went to the town Vārāṇasī (रथेनैकेन  … । जगाम … पुरीं वाराणसीं प्रति) 1. 96. 3-4; all the Kṣatriyas had then assem-bled at Kāśipurī for the स्वयंवर 5. 175. 17; Bhīṣma's victory over the Kṣatriyas, single-handed, at Kāśīpurī referred to by Saṃjaya while reporting Bhīṣma's fall in the war (जिगायैकरथेनैव काशिपुर्यां महा-रथः) 6. 14. 6; this incident that occurred in Vārāṇasī is referred to by Yudhiṣṭhira while lamenting over the death of Bhīṣma 12. 27. 9; also by Gaṅgā (समेतं पार्थिवं क्षत्रं काशिपुर्यां स्वयंवरे । विजित्यै-करथेनाजौ कन्यास् ता यो जहार ह ॥ ) 13. 154. 23; (2) Ambā told the ascetics that it was impossible for her to go back to her father's house in Kāśinagarī since she would be disrespected by her relatives (न शक्यं काशिनगरीं पुनर् गन्तुम् पितुर् गृहान्) 5. 174. 11; (3) Dhṛṣṭadyumna in a battle at Vārāṇasī felled down with a भल्ल arrow the son of Kāśirāja, who was greedy for women, from his chariot (this event is not reported in the epic) (यः (i. e. Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna) पुत्रं काशिराजस्य वाराणस्यां महारथम् । समरे स्त्रीषु गृध्यन्तं भल्लेनापहरद् रथात्) 7. 9. 56; (4) Kṛṣṇa had burnt the town Vārāṇasī which remained without a protector for a number of years (this incident is not reported in the epic (अनेन (i. e. by Kṛṣṇa) दग्धा वर्-षपूगान् विनाथा वाराणसी नगरी संब-भूव) 5. 47. 70. G. Past events: (1) The Hehayas attacked king Divodāsa who lived in Vārāṇasī, the city founded by him; Divodāsa came out of the town to fight with them 13. 31. 19-20; the battle lasted for a thousand days (दिनानां दशतीर् दश) (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 30. 21: दश-तिशब्दो ऽपि दशगुनितान् दश ब्रूते); with his army killed and his treasury empty, Divo-dāsa fled from the town (हतयोधस् ततो राजन् क्षीणकोशश् च भूमिपः । दिवोदासः पुरीम् हित्वा पलायनपरो ऽभवत् ॥ ) 13. 31. 21-22; (2) A merchant of great fame, Tulādhāra by name, lived in Vārāṇasī; the Piśācas told Jājali that even Tulādhāra did not boast of himself as did Jājali 12. 253. 8; Jājali then decided to meet Tulādhāra, went to him at Vārāṇasī, and spoke to him (वाराणस्यां तुलाधारं समासाद्याब्रवीद् वचः) 12. 253. 11; when Jājali boasted again (that he knew धर्म: धर्मः प्राप्तो मयेति वै 12. 253. 41), an invisible voice from the sky told him that even Tulā-dhāra of Vārāṇasī did not deserve to speak in terms in which Jājali did (वाराणस्यां  … तुलाधारः प्रतिष्ठितः । सो ऽप्य् एवं नार्हते वक्तुम् यथा त्वं भाषसे द्विज ॥ ) 12. 253. 42-43; when Jājali went to Vārā-ṇasī he saw Tulādhāra selling goods (कालेन महतागच्छत् स तु वाराणसीं पुरीम्) 12. 253. 45; (3) Nārada told king Marutta that Saṃvarta, son of Aṅgiras and younger brother of Bṛhaspati, often visited Vārāṇasī (वाराणसीं तु नगरीम् अभीक्ष्णम् उपसे-वते); Marutta then went to Vārāṇasī and, as suggested by Nārada (14. 6. 23), placed a corpse at the gate of the town (पुर्या द्वारे); when Saṃvarta came to the gate (पुरीद्वारम् आविशत्) he saw the corpse and turned back (that is how Marutta recogni-zed Saṃvarta) 14. 6. 22, 27-29; (4) Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana once approached Maitreya in the family of an unchaste woman at Vārā-ṇasī; a conversation between the two on the virtues of gift (दान), austerities (तपस्) and learning (श्रुत, विद्या) took place there वाराणस्याम् उपातिष्ठन् मैत्रेयं स्वैरिणी-कुले) 13. 121. 3, 1-2 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 13. 120. 3: स्वम् ईरयति धर्माय प्रेरयति स्वैरिणी मुनिश्रेणी तस्याः कुले गृहे); (5) At Vārāṇasī the sage Jaigīṣavya once got with very little effort eight quali-ties of superhuman power from Śiva (म-माष्टगुणम् ऐश्वर्यं दत्तं भगवता पुरा । यत्नेनाल्पेन … वाराणस्याम्) 13. 18. 24. H. Simile: Vārāṇasī, founded by Divodāsa, was like Amarāvatī of Indra (शक्रस्येवामरावतीम्) 13. 31. 18.
विभोर्: Vibhor āyatanam nt.: Name of the holy resort (temple ?) of Viṣṇu. A. Location: In a holy forest, not very far from the sea and the तीर्थ known as Śūrpāraka (शूर्पारकं ददर्श ॥ तत्रो-दधेः कंचिद् अतीत्य देशम् … वनम् आससाद) 3. 118. 8-9; (स तत्र … विष्णोः … आयतनानि तेषां ददर्श) 3. 118. 10-11, 13. For B. Description and C. Epic event see Bhagasya āyatanam.
विराटनगर: Virāṭanagara nt.: Name of a city, the seat of the Matsya kingdom of Virāṭa; once the name occurs as Virāṭa, short for Virāṭanagara (?) 4. 1. 23; also Virāṭarāṣṭra appears for Vlrāṭanagara 1. 1. 114, (4. 1. 16). A. Description: (1) When the victory of Uttara was announced Virāṭa ordered that the main roads (of the town) be deco-rated with banners (राजमार्गाः क्रियन्तां मे पताकाभिर् अलंकृताः) 4. 63. 23; (2) The town of Matsyarāja shone as in a great festival and was filled with delighted and well nourished people (तन् महोत्सवसं-काशं हृष्टपुष्टजनावृतम् । नगरं मत्-स्यराजस्य शुशुभे ॥ ) 4. 67. 38; (3) The city is referred to as (i) नगर (besides in the name Virāṭanagara) 1. 2. 13; 4. 67. 38; 5. 63. 15: as (ii) पुर 4. 29. 10; 4. 32. 48, 49, 50 (विराटस्य पुराभ्याशे); 4. 66. 21; as (iii) राष्ट्र (धनंजयेन … विराटराष्ट्रे वसता) 1. 1. 114; (राष्ट्रे … विराटनृपतेः) 4. 1. 16. B. Epic event: (1) Dharma comforted Yudhiṣṭhira by telling him that the Pāṇḍavas, by his grace, would be able to live concealed, unknown to others, in the Virāṭanagara during the thirteenth year of their exile (विराटनगरे गूढा अविज्ञाताश् चरिष्यथ) 3. 298. 15, 18; (2) Jana-mejaya asked Vaiśaṃpāyana how his great-grandfathers lived during their अज्ञातवास in Virāṭanagara (कथं विराटनगरे … अज्ञातवासम् उषिताः) 4. 1. 1; (3) Yudhi-ṣṭhira suggested to the Pāṇḍavas to live in Virāṭanagara serving Virāṭa (विराटनगरे  … कुर्वन्तस् तस्य कर्माणि) 4. 1. 14; (4) Arjuna asked Yudhiṣṭhira what kind of work he would do for Virāṭa while living in his राष्ट्र (कठं कर्म राष्ट्रे तस्य, करिष्यसि । विराटनृपतेः) 4. 1. 16; (राष्ट्रे, however, may mean here ‘kingdom’); (5) Bhīma was asked how he would amuse him-self in Virāṭa (nagara) (वृकोदर विराटे त्वं रंस्यसे केन कर्मणा) 4. 1. 23; (6) Nakula told his brothers that he would tell the people of Virāṭanagara that his name was Granthika and that he was expert in horse-training (ये माम् आमन्त्र-यिष्यन्ति विराटनगरे जनाः । तेभ्य एवं प्रवक्ष्यामि) 4. 3. 2-4; (7) After reaching Virāṭanagara, where the Pāṇḍavas lived in disguise, they hid their arms on a large Śamī tree in the cremation ground (विराटनग-रं गत्वा श्मशाने विपुलां शमीम् । दृष्ट्वा संनिदधुस् तत्र पाण्डवा आयुधान्य् उत ॥ यत्र प्रविश्य नगरं छद्मभिर् न्यव-सन्त ते) 1. 2. 130-131; (8) Suśarman of the Trigartas proposed to the Kauravas to oppress the town (of Virāṭa) and carry away his thousands of cows (प्रतिपीड्य पुरं बलात्) 4. 29. 10; Duryodhana sugge-sted that first Suśarsman should rush on Virāṭanagara and capture the cows (ते यात्वा विराटनगरं प्रति) 4. 29. 25; (9) When Suśarman carried away the cows of Virāṭa, the chief cowherd went to the town and reported the raid to Virāṭa (गोपाः पुरम् अथाव्रजत्) 4. 30. 4; the Matsya army, led by Virāṭa, came out of the town to fight with the Trigartas (निर्याय नगरात्) 4. 31. 1; when Virāṭa, with the help of the Pāṇḍa-vas, defeated Suśarman and his army he ordered his messengers to go to the town and declare his victory (आचक्षध्वं पुरं गत्वा संग्रामे विजयं मम); he wanted the princes, the courtesans and the players on musical instruments to come out of his town to meet him (पर्यागच्छन्तु मे पुरात्) 4. 32. 48-49; accordingly the messen-gers went at sunrise to the town of Virāṭa and declared the king's victory (विराटस्य पुराभ्याशे) 4. 32. 50; after defeating the Trigartas, Virāṭa entered the town with the Pāṇḍavas (विराटः … प्राविशन् नगरम्) 4. 63. 1; (10) After the defeat of the Kau-ravas, Arjuna told Uttara that they both would return to Virāṭanagara in the after-noon (ततो ऽपराण्हे यास्यामो विराटनग-रं प्रति) 4. 62. 9; (11) The messengers sent by Uttara reached Virāṭanagara and announced his victory 4. 63. 17; (12) Virāṭa, delighted to know the identity of the Pāṇḍavas, offered to Yudhiṣṭhira his whole kingdom, with the army, treasury, and the town (राज्यं च सर्वं विससर्ज तस्मै सदण्डकोशं सपुरं महात्मा) 4. 66. 21; (13) The town of the Matsya king, full of delighted and nourished people, shone as in a great festival (तन् महोत्स-वसंकाशं हृष्टपुष्टजनावृतम् । नगरं मत्स्यराजस्य शुशुभे) 4. 67. 38; (14) The Pāṇḍavas' stay in Virāṭanagara was like their entering another womb (विराटनगरे योन्यन्तरगतैर् इव) 5. 20. 11; 9. 55. 30; (cf. 4. 66. 10); (15) Arjuna's defeating the Kauravas single-handed when he lived in Virāṭanagara is referred to on various occasions: (i) by Dhṛtarāṣṭra (धनं-जयेनैकरथेन भग्नान् । विराटराष्ट्रे वसता) 1. 1. 114 (विराटराष्ट्र however, may mean here kingdom of विराट); (ii) by Vāsudeva in his message to Dhṛta-rāṣṭra through Saṃjaya 5. 58. 26-27; (iii) by Dhṛtarāṣṭra while speaking to Duryo-dhana 5. 63. 14, 15 (तस्मिन् नगरे); (iv) by Kṛṣṇa while speaking to Duryodhana 5. 122. 53; (v) by Bhīṣma and Droṇa while reminding Duryodhana of the past incident 5. 136. 6; (vi) by Bhīṣma once again while replying to Duryodhana (the stanzas also refer to the depriving of the Kaurava heroes of their upper garments) 6. 94. 8-9; (vii) by Kṛpa while remind-ing Karṇa 7. 133. 17; (viii) by Śalya when he asked Karṇa why he did not kill Arjuna at Virāṭanagara although he then enjoyed the protection of Bhīṣma, Droṇa and others 8. 28. 56; (16) Arjuna's stay at Virāṭanagara as Bṛhannaḍā wearing a braid mentioned by Ulūka while delivering Duryodhana's message to the Pāṇḍavas (धृता हि वेणी पार्थेन विराटनगरे तदा) 5. 158. 31; (17) The enmity formed by the five Trigarta brothers with Arjuna at Virāṭanagara (based on the incident of the cow-raid) referred to by Bhīṣma while giving his estimate of the heroes (त्रिगर्ता भ्रातरः पञ्च … । कृतवैराश् च पार्थेन विराटनगरे तदा) 5. 163. 9; (18) When Bhīṣma routed the army of the Pāṇḍavas, Kṛṣṇa reminded Arjuna of his declaration at Virāṭanagara that he would kill Bhīṣma, Droṇa and others in the battle (यत् पुरा कथितं वीर त्वया … विराटनगरे) 6. 102. 32; (19) Facing Karṇa in the battle, Bhīma remembered the grief they had suffered at Virāṭanagara (विराटनगरे … प्राप्तं दुःखम्) 7. 107. 9; he remember-ed the same when he faced Duryodhana (दुःखं च यत् प्राप्तम् … विराटनगरे चैव) 9. 55. 30; (20) Karṇa admitted Bhīma's strength of arms exhibited by him in killing Kīcaka and his followers at Virāṭa-nagara (विराटनगरे तदा । … केवलं बाहु-संश्रयत् … कीचकः सगणो हतः) 8. 34. 19; the same incident referred to by Drau-padī when she exhorted Bhīma to kill Aśvatthāman 10. 11. 24.
विश्रवसः: Viśravasaḥ niketaḥ m.: The residence of the sage Viśravas. Situated on the holy river Narmadā (प्रत्यक्स्रोता नदी पुण्या नर्मदा तत्र … । निकेतः ख्यायते पुण्यो यत्र विश्रवसो मुनेः) 3. 87. 2-3; described as holy (पुण्य) 3. 87. 3; Kubera, the lord of riches, was born in this निकेत (जज्ञे ध-नपतिर् यत्र कुबेरः) 3. 87. 3.
विश्वामित्राश्रम: Viśvāmitrāśrama m.: The hermitage of Viśvāmitra. A. Location: On the western bank of Sarasvatī (आश्रमः … पश्चिमश् चासीद् विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः … यत्र पूजयित्वा सरस्वतीम्) 9. 41. 4, 6. B. Events: (1) Viśvāmitra asked Sarasvatī to bring to him Vasiṣṭha whose आश्रम was on the opposite bank for the wanted to kill Vasiṣṭha 9. 41. 16, 18; Sarasvatī did accordingly by with-drawing a portion of her opposite bank (कूलापहारम् अकरोत् 9. 41. 27) and took Vasiṣṭha to the आश्रम of Viśvāmitra (वेगेनोवाह तं विप्रं विश्वामित्राश्रमं प्रति) 9. 41. 32; Sarasvatī then carried back Vasiṣṭha from Viśvāmitra's आश्रम to his own आश्रम to the east 9. 41. 34; (2) Formerly, at the junction of Tretā and Dvā-para, during a period of severe drought which lasted for twelve years, Viśvāmitra and other sages left their hermitages and, home-less, they ran about here and there 12. 139. 13, 26; (आश्रमान् संपरित्यज्य पर्यधा-वन्न् इतस् ततः । विश्वामित्रो ऽथ … अनिके-तनः । क्षुधापरिगतो धीमान् समन्तात् पर्यधावत ॥ ) 12. 139. 25-26.
विष्णोर्: Viṣṇor āyatanam nt.: Name of a holy resort (temple ?) of Viṣṇu. A. Location: In a holy forest, not very far from the sea and the तीर्थ known as Śūrpāraka (शूर्पारकं ददर्श ॥ तत्रोद-धेः कंचिद् अतीत्य देशं … वनम् आस-साद) 3. 118. 8-9; (स तत्र … विष्णोः … आयतनानि तेषां ददर्श) 3. 118. 10-11, 13. For B. Description and C. Epic event see Bhagasya āyatanam.

Viṣṇor āśramaḥ m.: The आश्रम of Viṣṇu. A. Location: From Kurukṣetra, Bala-rāma went to the आश्रम of Viṣṇu (कुरु-क्षेत्रं ततो दृष्ट्वा … आश्रमं (विष्णोः) … अगमत्) 9. 53. 1; by the side of Himavant (पार्श्वे हिमवतः) 9. 53. 9. B. Descrip-tion: Holy (पुण्य) 9. 53. 2, 9, having holy marks (पुण्यलक्षण) 9. 53. 3; heavenly (दिव्य) 9. 53. 1; very large (सुमहन्त्) 9. 53. 1; excellent (प्रवर), (आश्रमवर) 9. 53. 3; it was full of trees such as Madhūka, mango, Plakṣa, banyan, Ciri, Bilva, Panasa, and Arjuna 9. 53. 2; C. History: On enquiry, the sages told Bala-rāma that the आश्रम formerly belonged to Viṣṇu; god Viṣṇu, in bygone days, practised excellent austerities in that आश्रम; all ancient sacrifices were performed according to the rites by Viṣṇu in the आश्रम (शृणु विस्तरशो राम यस्यायं पूर्वम् आश्रमः ॥ अत्र विष्णुः पुरा देवस् तप्तवांस् तप उत्तमम् । अत्रास्य विधिवद् यज्ञाः सर्वे वृत्ताः सनातनाः ॥ ) 9. 53. 4-5. D. Past event: In this आश्रम the daughter of Śāṇḍilya who observed chastity obtained perfection by practising austerities; after enjoying in the आश्रम the fruit of an अश्वमेध sacrifice, she was absorbed in meditation and went to heaven (अत्रैव ब्राह्मणी सिद्धा कौमारब्रह्मचारिणी । योगयुक्ता दिवं याता तपःसिद्धा … ॥ ब-भूव … शाण्डिल्यस्य … सुता ॥ सा तु प्राप्य परं योगं गता स्वर्गम् अनुत्तमम् । भुक्त्वाश्रमे ऽश्वमेधस्य फलं … । गता स्वर्गं महाभागा ॥ ) 9. 53. 6-8. E. Epic event: Balarāma paid respects to the sages and from that आश्रम he mounted the mountain (आरुरुहे ऽचलम्) 9. 53. 9.
वीराश्रम: Vīrāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम। One who visits Kumāra living in the Vīrāśrama gets without doubt the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice (कुमारम् अभि-गत्वा च वीराश्रमनिवासिनम् । अश्वमेधम् अवाप्नोति नरो नास्त्य् अत्र संशयः ॥ ) 3. 82. 126.
वृकस्थल: Vṛkasthala nt.: Name of a village. A. Location: On way from Upapla-vya to Hāstinapura (उपप्लव्याद् अथायान्-तम् (केशवम्) 5. 82. 18; (उपप्लव्याद् इह क्षत्तर् उपयातो जनार्दनः । वृकस्थले निवसति स च प्रातर् इहेष्यति ॥ ) 5. 84. 1. B. Characterized as ग्राम: (ग्रामान् पञ्च) 5. 70. 16; (पञ्च ग्रामा वृता मया) 5. 70. 14; (पञ्च नस् तात दीयन्तां ग्रामा इति) 5. 80. 7; (तस्मिन् ग्रामे) 5. 82. 25; (ग्रामे वृकस्थले) 5. 83. 16. C. Epic events: (1) Vṛkasthala was one of the five villages in lieu of which Yudhiṣṭhira was prepared to come to terms with the Kauravas (the other three villages actu-ally named being Kuśasthala. Āsandī and Vāraṇāvata)—this was mentioned by Yudhiṣṭhira first to Saṃjaya 5. 31. 19, and then again in his message to the Kauravas through Kṛṣṇa 5. 70. 15; also referred to by Draupadī in her address to Kṛṣṇa 5. 80. 7; (2) Kṛṣṇa, on his way to Hāstinapura, from Upaplavya, reached Vṛkasthala in the evening and performed there evening rites; he decided to stay there for the night (वृक-स्थलं समासाद्य … प्रकीर्णरश्माव् आदित्ये विमले लोहितायति ॥ अवतीर्य रथात् तूर्णं  … संध्याम् उपविवेश ह) 5. 82. 20-21; (इह वत्स्यामहे क्षपाम्) 5. 82. 23; the people of the village Vṛkasthala arranged for Kṛṣṇa's stay (चक्रुर् आवसथं नराः); the principal Brāhmaṇas of the village went to Kṛṣṇa and worshipped him according to the rules and gave him blessings (तस्मिन् ग्रामे प्रधानास् तु य आसन् ब्राह्मणा नृप । अभिगम्य … हृषीकेशं … पूजां चक्रुर् यथान्यायम् आशीर्मङ्गलसं-युताम् ॥ ); as requested by the Brāhmaṇas, Kṛṣṇa visited their houses and returned; he fed them and dined with them and spent the night happily there (अवसत् तां क्षपां सुखम्) 5. 82. 24-29; Duryodhana had constructed a hall in the village Vṛkasthala for Kṛṣṇa's stay; but Kṛṣṇa ignored this सभा (as well as others in other villages) and proceeded to the house of the Kurus (विशेषतश् च वासार्थं सभां ग्रामे वृकस्थले । विदधे कौरवो राजा॑ … ताः सभाः … असमीक्ष्यैव दाशार्ह उपायात् कुरुसद्म तत्) 5. 83. 16, 18; when Kṛṣṇa started for the town (Hāstinapura), people of Vṛkasthala took his leave and returned to their village 5. 87. 2.
वृन्दाटक: Vṛndāṭaka nt.: Name of a town. Located to the west of Hāstinapura; it was one of the towns subjugated by Nakula in his expedition to the west (निर्-याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम् 2. 29. 2) before the Rājasūya (तथा वृन्दाटकं पुरम् । … वशे चक्रे) 2. 29. 10.
वृष्ण्यन्धकपुर: Vṛṣṇyandhakapura nt.: Another name of Dvārakā.
