When Śālva beseiged Dvārakā no one could go out or enter Vṛṣṇyandhakapura without stamped permission (न चामुद्रो ऽभिनिर्याति न चामुद्रः प्रवेश्यते । वृष्ण्यन्धकपुरे राजंस् तदा सौभसमा-गमे) 3. 16. 19; army having many ele-phants and horses was stationed along all the roads and squares of the town (अनु रथ्-यासु सर्वासु चत्वरेषु च कौरव । बलं बभूव राजेन्द्र प्रभूतगजवाजिमत्) 3. 16. 20. [See Dvārakā]
वेत्रकीयगृह: Vetrakīyagṛha nt.: Name of a place, another name of Ekacakrā (?) The wife of the Brāhmaṇa told Kuntī that the king who had agreed to give to the demon Baka as वेतन a cart-full of rice, two buffaloes and the man who took the cart to him lived in Vetrakīyagṛha; the king had not acted justly towards his subjects (वेत्रकीयगृहे राजा नायं नयम् इहास्थि-तः) 1. 148. 9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 160. 9: वेत्रकीयगृहे स्थानविशेषे); Kirmīra told Yudhiṣṭhira that he had for long sought to kill Bhīma since the latter had killed his (Kirmīra's) brother Baka in Vetrakīyagṛha (अनेन हि मम भ्राता बको विनिहतः प्रियः । वेत्रकीयगृहे) 3. 12. 30 (Nī. in Bom. Ed. 3. 11. 31 reads वैत्रकीयवने and identifies it with Ekacakrā: वैत्रकीयवने एकचक्रायाम्). [See Ekacakrā]
वैखानसाश्रम: Vaikhānasāśrama, Vaikhānasānāmāśramaḥ  m.: The आश्रम where the Vai-khānasas lived. A. Location: Situated in the north (अस्यां दिशि वरिष्ठायाम् उत्तरायाम्) 5. 109. 3. B. Holiness: One of the holy and sanctified places in the west mentioned by Dhaumya (प्रतीच्याम् … दिशि । यानि तत्र पवित्राणि पुण्यान्य् आयतनानि च) 3. 87. 1; the आश्रम was dear to the Vaikhānasa sages who had obtained perfection (वैखा-नसानां सिद्धानां ऋषीणाम् आश्रमः प्रि-यः) 3. 87. 13. C. Past event: It was poin-ted out by Suparṇa to Gālava (अत्र वैखा-नसाश्रमः) 5. 109. 9.
वैदिश: Vaidiśa nt.: Name of a town (= Vidiśā ?) In ancient times a dialogue took place between a vulture and a jackal which was narrated by Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣṭhira (शृणु पार्थ यथावृत्तम् इतिहासं पुरातनम् । गृध्रजम्बूकसंवादं यो वृत्तो वैदिशे पुरा) 12. 149. 1.
वैश्रवणस्य: Vaiśravaṇasya sadman nt.: See Mahen-drasya sadman.
व्यासाश्रम: Vyāsāśrama1 m.: Hermitage of Vyāsa. A. Location: On the slope of the mountain Himavant (हिमवत्पृष्ठे) 12. 314. 30; to the east, on a lonely spot on the slope of the mountain (ऐन्द्रीं तु दिशम् आस्थाय शैलराजस्य धीमतः । विविक्ते पर्वततटे … । तत्राश्रमपदं … पितुः) 12. 314. 23, 25. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) and best (उत्तम) 12. 314. 25. C. Epic events: (1) Vyāsa was surrounded by his pupils Sumantu, Vaiśaṃpāyana, Jaimini and Paila in the आश्रम; he taught them the Vedas 12. 314. 23, 25; (2) Śuka, after his dialogue with Janaka, went to see his father in the आश्रम to the east of Himavant 12. 314. 23, 25; Vyāsa saw his son arriving through air; Śuka reported to Vyāsa about his dialogue with Janaka 12. 314. 26-27, 29; Vyāsa taught the Vedas also to his son 12. 314. 30; (3) Once Vyāsa's pupils requested him that he should not accept any one, other than his four pupils and his son Śuka, as his pupil (षष्ठः शिष्यो न ते ख्यातिं गच्छेद् अत्र प्रसीद नः ॥ चत्वा-रस् ते वयं शिष्या गुरुपुत्रश् च पञ्च-मः) 12. 314. 37-38; Vyāsa then told his pupils, living with him in the आश्रम, to go down on the earth and propagate the Vedas (वेदो विस्तार्यताम् अयम्); the Vedas should be taught to all the four Varṇas (श्रावयेच् चतुरो वर्णान्); he explained to them the procedure of Vedic teaching (एतद् वः सर्वम् आख्यातम् स्वाध्यायस्य विधिं प्रति) 12. 314. 39-49; accordingly the pupils expressed their wish to leave (the आश्रम on) the mountain and go down on the earth to propagate the Vedas (शैलाद् अस्मान् महीं गन्तुं काङ्क्षितं नो महामुने । वेदान् अनेकधा कर्तुम्) 12. 315. 4; when permitted by Vyāsa they (left the आश्रम) and descended from the mountain to the earth (जग्मुः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा व्या-सं … । अवतीर्य महीम्) 12. 315. 7-10; (4) Nārada, who arrived at the आश्रम, saw Vyāsa, sitting alone, and engaged in meditation and not reciting the Vedas (तं ददर्शाश्रमपदे) 12. 315. 11-12; as suggested by Nārada, Vyāsa and his son Śuka recited the Vedas loudly 12. 315. 22-23; Vyāsa explained to Śuka why he stopp-ed Vedic recitation when there was a strong gust of wind (वातो ऽतिमात्रं प्रववौ) 12. 315. 24; later he asked Śuka to continue the recitation and himself went (from the आश्रम) to Vyomagaṅgā (उक्त्वा पुत्रम् अधीष्वेति व्योमगङ्गाम् अयात् तदा) 12. 315. 57; (5) When instructed by Nārada, Śuka took leave of Vyāsa and left him (in the आश्रम) to ascend to the mountain top (पितरं संपरित्यज्य जगाम … ॥ गिरि-पृष्ठं समारुह्य) 12. 318. 60-63; 12. 319. 1; Vyāsa (then left the आश्रम and) followed his son (तं प्रक्रमन्तम् आज्ञाय पिता … पृष्ठतो ऽनुससार ह) 12. 320. 18.

Vyāsāśrama2 m.: Another आश्रम of Vyāsa. A. Location: On way from Indra-prastha to Hāstinapura (?) 16. 8. 74 (see the next section). B. Epic events: (1) After establishing Vajra at Indraprastha, Arjuna, on his way to Hāstinapura, saw Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana in his आश्रम (कृष्णद्वै-पायनं राजन् ददर्शासीनम् आश्रमे) 16. 8. 74: Arjuna entered the आश्रम of Vyāsa and saw the holy sage sitting in a solitary place; when consoled by Vyāsa over the destruction of the Yādavas, he left for Hāstinapura (प्रविशन्न् अर्जुनो राजन्न् आश्र-मं सत्यवादिनः । ददर्शासीनम् एकान्ते मुनिं सत्यवतीसुतम्) 16. 9. 1; (अनुज्ञातो ययौ पार्थो नगरं नागसाह्वयम्) 16. 9. 37; (2) After meeting Dhṛtarāṣṭra and others, Aśvatthāman went to Vyāsāśrama (द्रौणिर् व्यासाश्रमं ययौ) 11. 10. 21.
वक्र: Vakra m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (वक्रा वक्रभयाः) 6. 10. 43.
वक्रभय: Vakrabhaya m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (वक्रा वक्रभयाः) 6. 10. 43 (For other references see Vakra).
वङ्ग: Vaṅga m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people; the country is also referred to as Viṣaya (2. 41. 9); sometimes Vaṅga is mentioned along with Aṅga and Kaliṅga. A. Location: (1) Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्-वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37. 5; (अङ्गा वङ्गाः कलिङ्गाश् च) 6. 10. 44; (2) In the east 1. 207. 5 (see Epic events No. 2 below); (3) Vaṅga people said to be born on the bays of ocean and along the rivers (समुद्र-निष्कुटे जाताः परिसिन्धु च मानवाः) 2. 47. 9 (Nī. however, on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 11: समुद्रसमीपस्थनिष्कुटे गृहोद्याने); the Aśvamedha horse of Yudhiṣṭhira went from Magadha, along the (eastern) sea coast, to Vaṅga, Puṇḍra and Kerala countries. B. Description and characteristics: Diffi-cult to be conquered (दुर्जय) 8. 5. 18; their warriors fought while riding elephants (गजयोधिन् 6. 87. 14; 8. 17. 2; गज-युद्धेषु कुशलाः 8. 17. 3; also see Epic events No. 4, 9, and 10 below); they lived on crops produced in forest without plough-ing by rain water or produced by river water (इन्द्रकृष्टैर् वर्तयन्ति धान्यैर् नदीमुखैश् च ये) 2. 47. 9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 11; इन्द्रकृष्टैः इन्द्रेणैवा-कृष्टैः न तु कर्षणादिक्षेत्रियकयत्ना-पेक्षैः वनधान्यैः वृष्ट्यभावे तु नदी-मुखैः नदीप्रभवैः). C. Epic events; (1) Caturyu (?) Bhoja, king of Vaṅgas, Puṇḍras and Kirātas was known to the worlds as Pauṇḍraka Vāsudeva 2. 13. 19-20; (2) Arjuna during the period of his exile, visited all the तीर्थस् in Aṅga, Vaṅga and Kaliṅga countries in the east (प्राचीम् दिशम् अभिप्रेप्सुः) 1. 207. 5, 9; (3) Vaṅgas brought tribute in the form of various jewels, goats, sheep, cows, gold, donkeys, camels, various kinds of blankets and wine produced from fruits (फलजं मधु) for the Rājasūya; but they were stopped at the gate 2. 47. 10-11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 13: फलजं मधूकादि-जातीयम्); their Kṣatriyas brought wealth in hundreds for Yudhiṣṭhira (आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 15; they brought fine cloth, silk, silk (or cotton ?) garments, पत्रोर्ण and covers (दुकूलं कौशिकं चैव पत्रोर्णं प्रावरान् अपि) 2. 48. 17 (Nī. on 2. 51. 3: और्णान् मेष-रोमजान्); when asked to give more to get entrance, each one gave one thousand elephants 2. 48. 18, 20 (description of elephants 19-20); the king of Vaṅgas was among those who, subdued by the fear of the lustre of Pāṇḍavas' weapons, acted as servants in the sacrifice (यज्ञे ते परिवेष-कान्) 3. 48. 18, 22; (4) On the eighth day of war, when Duryodhana attacked Ghaṭo-tkaca he was followed by the king of Vaṅgas with ten thousand elephant-fighters (गजयोधिनः); the war between the Rākṣasas of Ghaṭotkaca and the elephant-fighters from Vaṅgas described in 6. 87. 10, 13-14; (5) During Saṃjaya's report after the death of Droṇa, Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, at one stage, while recounting Kṛṣṇa's past exploits, mentioned his victory over Vaṅgas 7. 10. 15; (6) On the twelfth day, Dhṛtarāṣṭra mentioned Vaṅgas among those who had joined the army of Kauravas 7. 23. 7; (7) In the night war (between the 14th and the 15th day), Yudhiṣṭhira killed many Vaṅgas 7. 136. 3; (8) When Karṇa's death was reported to Dhṛṭarāṣṭra, he remembered that Karṇa had once defeated Vaṅgas in battle and made them pay tribute (यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 19-20 (reference to Karṇa's Digvijaya before the Vaiṣṇavayajña of Duryodhana 3. 241. 29-32; 3. App. I. 24. 42); (9) On the sixteenth day, Vaṅgas and others riding elephants, who were like the elephants of Indra, rushed at Arjuna to kill him; Arjuna cut off the armours, the vitals and trunks of the elephants and also their controllers (अथ द्विपैर् देवपतिद्विपाभैर् … कलिङ्ग-वङ्ग° … । तेषां द्विपानां विचकर्त पार्थो वर्माणि मर्माणि करान् नियन्तॄन्) 8. 12. 59-60; on the same day, incited by Duryodhana, Vaṅgas and others, riding elephants, attacked Dhṛṣṭadyumna to kill him; they showered arrows, तोमरस्, नाराच arrows on him 8. 17. 2-3; other Pāṇḍava heroes joined the battle; the battle described in 8. 17. 5 ff.; Sātyaki killed the king of Vaṅgas and his elephant 8. 17. 11; (10) On the seventeenth day, Arjuna told Yudhiṣṭhira that Bhīma alone who had killed Kaliṅgas, Vaṅgas and Aṅgas as also their elephants had the right to blame him 8. 49. 79; (11) The sacrificial horse of the Aśvamedha went from Magadha, along the seacoast, to Vaṅga, Puṇḍra and Kerala countries; Arjuna conquered there many Mlecchas 14. 83. 29-30. D. Some per-sons referred to as the chief or the king of Vaṅgas: (1) Karṇa called वङ्गाङ्ग-विषयाध्यक्ष 2. 41. 9; (2) A king, not named, referred to as king of Vaṅgas: (i) वङ्गराज 2. 27. 21; (ii) राज्ञा वङ्गेन 6. 88. 8; (iii) वङ्गानाम् अधिपः 6. 88. 6; (iv) वङ्गानाम् ईश्वरः 6. 88. 10.
वत्स: Vatsa m. (pl.), Vatsabhūmi f. (sg.): Name of a country and its people. A. Location: In the east, somewhat to the north (see Epic event No. 1 below). B. Description (1) of its warriors: Deter-mined to win victory they were prepared to give away their lives (त्यक्तात्मानो जये धृताः) 5. 52. 1; valorous (पराक्रान्त) 5. 52. 2; (2) of their capital town: pleasing (रम्या) 13. 31. 12; the country was visited by Siddhas and Cāraṇas (सिद्धचारणसेविता) and was the resort of holy and magnanimous ascetics (आश्रमं पुण्यशीलानां तापसानां मनस्विनाम्) 5. 187. 23. C. Epic events: (1) Bhīma in his expedition before the Rājasūya first went to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1; 2. 23. 9), and then to the north, and conquered with force the land of the Vatsas (प्रययाव् उत्तरामुखः । वत्सभूमिं च कौन्तेयो विजिग्ये बलवान् बलात् ॥ ) 2. 27. 9; (2) Dhṛtarāṣṭra reminded Saṃjaya that he had mentioned the kings of Vatsabhūmi among the allies of Pāṇḍavas (अभिसरास् तेषाम् … त्वम् एव हि … आचक्षीथाः … वत्स-भूमिपान्) 5. 52. 1-2; (3) After practis-ing severe austerites on the river Yamunā, Ambā went to Vatsabhūmi; she bathed there day and night in the holy places; after visiting many तीर्थस् she returned to Vatsabhūmi where a half of her body became the river called Ambā; the river had water once a year, it was full of crocodiles and was difficult to cross 5. 187. 18-24; 34-35; 38-40; (4) On the second day of war, led by Nakula and Sahadeva, Vatsas and Nākulas were among those who stood at the left wing of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha (6. 46. 39; Krauñca 6. 47. 1) of Pāṇḍavas (वत्साश् च सह नाकुलैः । नकुलः सहदेवश् च वामं पार्श्वं समाश्रिताः) 6. 46. 51; (5) On the eleventh day, Dhṛtarāṣṭra while re-counting Kṛṣṇa's past exploits mentioned his victory over Vatsas 7. 10. 15; (6) On the sixteenth day, Dhṛtarāṣṭra remembered that Karṇa had formerly won victory over Vatsas and forced them to pay tribute (वत्सान् … यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा) 8. 5. 20 (reference to Karṇa's conquest of the earth before the Vaiṣnavayajña of Duryodhana 3. 241. 29, 32; 3. App. I. 24. 45-46. D. Past event: Hehaya and Tālajaṅgha, born in the line of Śaryāti, once ruled over Vatsas; Heha-yas killed in battle Haryaśva, king of Kāśi, and returned to the (capital) town of Vatsas (हेहयास् … । प्रतिजग्मुः पुरीं रम्यां वत्सानाम् … ॥ ) 13. 31. 7, 12. E. Yayāti referred to as king of Vatsas and Kāśīs (वत्सकाशीशः) 5. 113. 2; certain kings, not named, referred to as वत्स-भूमिप- 5. 52. 2.
वध्र: Vadhra m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (वध्राः करीषकाश् चापि) 6. 10. 54.
वनवासिन्: Vanavāsin m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the sou-thern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56, 5; भूषिका वनवासिनः 6. 10. 57.
वर्मक: Varmaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. Bhīma in his expedition to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिषं प्रति 2. 26. 1; 2. 23. 9) before the Rājasūya won over Varmakas through peaceful means (वर्मकांश् चैव सान्त्वेनैवाजयत् प्रभुः) 2. 27. 12.
वसाति: Vasāti, Vasātika, Vasātīya m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada (6. 18. 12, 14; 6. 114. 76-77) and its people; some of them desig-nated as Brahmavasātīya (7. 48. 8). A. Description: Their warriors: Brave (शूर) 5. 196. 3; 6. 18. 14; respected by brave (शूरसंमत) 7. 66. 39; strong, very strong (बलवन्त्) 6. 112. 107; (महा-बल) 5. 196. 3; chariot-fighters (महा-रथ) 6. 112. 107; ready to give up their lives (तनुत्यज्) 6. 18. 14; versed in Vedas, observing vows, doing duties, bearing scars of battles, desirous of winning other worlds (by death) in battles, having concentrated minds, trusting each other (सर्वे वेदविदः  … सर्वे सुचरितव्रताः । सर्वे कर्मकृतश् चैव सर्वे चाहवलक्षणाः ॥ आहवेषु पराल्̃ लोकाञ् जिगीषन्तो … । एकाग्रमनसः सर्वे श्रद्दधाना परस्य च ॥ ) 5. 196. 3-4. B. Characteristic: Karṇa while deriding Śalya mentioned Vasātis among those who were generally considered despicable (वसाति° … प्रायो विकुत्सिताः) 8. 30. 47. C. Epic events: (1) Vasāti Kṣatriyas had brought wealth in hundreds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो … ); when they were asked by the doorkeepers to give more tribute, each one gave one thousand elephants; they were then allowed to enter (कृतकाराः सुबलयस् ततो द्वारम् अवाप्स्यथ) 2. 48. 14, 18; the elephants they gave described in 2. 48. 19-20; (2) Listed by Yudhiṣṭhira among those who were gathered together by Duryodhana to fight with Pāṇḍavas; Yudhiṣṭhira asked Saṃjaya to enquire on his behalf about their well-being (तेषां सर्वेषां कुशलं तात पृच्छेः) 5. 30. 23-24; (3) As told by Duryodhana their armies, along with Śakuni, left Hāstinapura in the second division for Kurukṣetra (द्वितीये निर्ययुर् बले); before departure, they bathed, became pure, wore garlands and white garments, took up their arms, had the word स्वस्ति pronounced on them and offered oblations in fire 5. 196. 1-2, 7-8; (4) Vasātis mentioned among twelve Janapadas who with their large army of chariot-fighters (महता रथवं-शेन) were supposed to guard Bhīṣma 6. 18. 12; (5) On the second day of war, Vasātis, led by Śakuni in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas (6. 47. 10), were stationed to protect Droṇa (वसातयः । शकुनिश् च … भारद्वाजम् अपालयत्) 6. 47. 14; (6) On the third day, as directed by Bhīṣma, a large number of horse-riders, foot-soliders, and chariot-fighters of Vasātis attacked Arjuna (वाजिपादातरथौघजालैः) 6. 55. 74-75; (7) On the ninth day, though they were being killed by sharp arrows did not abandon Bhīṣma (संग्रामे नाजहुर् भीष्मं वध्यमानाः शितैः शरैः) 6. 102. 7; (8) On the tenth day, as directed by Duryodhana, their great chariot-fighters attacked Arjuna 6. 112. 102, 105, 107, 109; Vasātis mentioned among twelve Janapadas who though afflicted by arrows and pained due to wounds did not abandon Bhīṣma engaged in fighting with Arjuna at a time when the Kuru army fled (वयं … प्रद्रवाम महारणात् । … शरार्ता व्रणपीडिताः॑ संग्रामे न जहुर् भीष्मं युध्य-मानं किरीटिना ॥ ) 6. 114. 75-77; (9) On the twelfth day, Vasātis were among those who were posted at the ‘back’ (पृष्ठ) of the Suparṇavyūha of Kauravas (7. 19. 4, 11); (10) On the thirteenth day, Abhimanyu killed ten chariot-fighters of Brahmavasātīyas (पुनर् ब्रह्मवसातीयाञ् जघान रथिनो दश) 7. 48. 8; (11) On the fourteenth day at one stage Saṃjaya recalled that Vasātis were once defeated by Karṇa in battle (वसातयः … कर्णेन विजिताः पूर्वं सं-ग्रामे) 7. 66. 37, 39 (a reference to Karṇa's दिग्विजय before the Vaiṣṇavayajña of Duryodhana 3. 241. 29, 32; 3 App. I. 24. 28. 72); on that day Vasātis and chariot-fighters totalling ten thousand tried to obstruct the way of Arjuna bent on killing Jayadratha; a fierce battle was fought (धनंजयम् अवारयन्; जयद्रथ-वधप्रेप्सुं … न्यवारयन्त सहिताः) 7. 66. 36-43; the same day when Śrutāyudha was killed by Arjuna Vasātis and other warriors, six thousand strong (तेषां षष्टि-शतान्), showered arrows on him; when Arjuna shot arrows, afraid, they ran away; but they returned and surrounded Arjuna on all sides; Arjuna cut off their heads and arms 7. 68. 2-5; after the death of Jaya-dratha, Duryodhana while blaming Droṇa mentioned Vasātis among those who, for his sake, got killed while fighting with Arjuna (हता मदर्थं संग्रामे युध्य-माना किरीटिना) 7. 125. 31-32; (12) During the night war (14th-15th day), Yudhiṣṭhira killed Vasātikas and others (बाह्लीकान् सवसातिकान्) 7. 132. 24; (13) On the fifteenth day, Dhṛṣṭadyumna dispersed (व्यधमत्) Vasātis and others who were protecting Droṇa 7. 165. 24; (14) On the seventeenth day, Kṛṣṇa, to encourage Arjuna, reminded him that in the past seventeen days of war (अथ सप्तदशाहानि वर्तमानस्य भारत 8. 51. 2) he had killed armies of Vasātis, along with their horses and elephants, when they fought with him 8. 51. 16; (15) On the night of the seventeenth day (निशि 8. 1. 25), Saṃjaya while reporting the death of Karṇa men-tioned that two thousand fighting Vasātis were killed in the war (वसातयो … द्वि-साहस्राः प्रहारिणः) 8. 4. 36. D. Some persons referred to as those belonging to Vasātis: A certain hero of Vasātis, not named, designated as वसातीय 7. 43. 8; and then as वसात्य 7. 43. 11.
वस्त्रप: Vastrapa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Their Kṣatriyas brought wealth in hundreds for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (वस्त्रपाः पह्लवैः सह । आहार्षुः क्ष-त्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 14, 16.
वाटधान: Vāṭadhāna m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (वाहीका वाटधानाश् च) 6. 10. 45; situated to the west of Indraprastha (see epic event No. 1. below); beyond Pañcanada and Kurujāṅgala and adjacent to the Yāmuna mountain (see epic event No. 2 below). B. Description: The country was very ex-tensive and having ample wealth and grains (सुविस्तीर्णः प्रभूतधनधान्यवान्) 5. 19. 30-31; rich in cattle (गोमन्त्) 2. 45. 24 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 49. 24; वाटाः क्षेत्रादि-वृत्तयः तासां धाना अभिनवोद्भेदो येषां ते इति व्यधिकरणो बहुव्रीहिः । सस्यादिसंपन्नक्षेत्रादिवृत्तिमन्त इत्य् अर्-थः). C. Epic events: (1) In his expedition to the west of the Khāṇḍava-prastha (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रती-चीम् अभितो दीशम् 2. 29. 2; 2. 23. 10), Nakula subjugated the Vāṭadhāna Brāh-maṇas (वशे चक्रे … वाटधानान् द्विजान् अथ); hundreds of Vāṭadhāna Brāhmaṇas (ब्राह्मणा वाटधानाश् च … शतसंघ-शः) brought as tribute for the Rājasūya thirty billions (of wealth) (त्रैखर्वं बलिम्), but were stopped at the gate; when they, in addition, gave bright water-pots of gold they were allowed to enter (कमण्डलून् उपादाय जातरूपमयाञ् शुभान् … प्रवेशं लेभिरे ततः) 2. 45. 24-25; (2) Since there was not enough room in Hāstinapura to accommodate the army of Kauravas, it spread beyond Pañcanada and Kurujāṅgala to Vāṭadhāna country and Yāmuna mountain 5. 19. 30-31; (3) On the third day of the war, Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa along with Vāṭadhānas and others formed the ‘head’ (शीर्षम्) of the Garuḍavyūha of Kauravas 6. 52. 2, 4; (4) At night of the fifteenth day (निशि 7. 1. 7), when Droṇa's death was reported to Dhṛtarāṣṭra he men-tioned Kṛṣṇa's victory over Vāṭadhānas among his exploits 7. 10. 17; (5) On the seventeenth day, Kṛṣṇa, to encourage Arjuna, reminded him that during the past sixteen days of war (अद्य सप्तदशाहान्त् 8. 51. 2) he had killed large armies of Vāṭadhāna Brāhmaṇas and other Kṣatriyas along with their horses and elephants and broken their chariots (व्रात्यानां वाट-धानानाम् … महासेना ब्रह्मक्षत्रस्य भारत । … साश्वरथद्विपाः) 8. 51. 16-17. D. Vāṭadhāna, name of one of the kings who were born from the Gaṇa called Krodhavaśa (गणः क्रोधवशो नाम … ततः संजज्ञिरे वीराः क्षिताव् इह नराधि-पाः) 1. 59. 31; 1. 61. 54; (वाटधानो ऽथ गोमुखः) 1. 61. 58 (Has this king's name any relationship with the Janapada named Vāṭadhāna ?).
वातजाम: Vātajāma m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada (?). Mentioned by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (वातजाम-रथोरगाः) 6. 10. 53 (It is not clear how the compound वातजामरथोरग is to be understood) [See Uraga and Rathoraga].
वानरास्य: Vānarāsya m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (वानरास्याः प्रवा-हाश् च) 6. 10. 43.
वानायु: Vānāyu m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas) of Bhāṛata-varṣa (वानायवो दशापार्श्वाः) 6. 10. 54; (for other references see the above entry).
वासुदेव: Vāsudeva m. (pl.): Designation of Vṛṣṇis in general.
वाहीक: Vāhīka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the Northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (वाहीका वाटधानाश् च) 6. 10. 45.
विकर्ण: Vikarṇa m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the second day of war, Duryo-dhana, supported by Vikarṇas and others, offered protection to the army of Śakuni in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas (अश्वा-तकैर् विकर्णैश् च) 6. 47. 10, 15-16.
विकल्प: Vikalpa m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा … दक्षिणा) 6. 10. 56, 5; (विकल्पा मूषकास् तथा) 6. 10. 57.
विकुञ्ज: Vikuñja m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the third day of war, Vikuñjas and others, led by Bṛhadbala, were stationed at the left wing of the Garuḍavyūha (6. 52. 2-3) of the Kauravas (विकुञ्जाश् च … । बृहद्बलेन सहिता वामं पक्षम् उपाश्रिताः (6. 52. 9).
विदर्भ: Vidarbha m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people; a king of the country referred to as Vaidarbha and a princess as Vaidarbhī. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (विधर्भानूपवासिकाः) 6. 10. 42; called राष्ट्र (sg.) 12. 264. 3. B. Description: Excelling others in the observance of धर्म, best (राष्ट्रे धर्मोत्तरे श्रेष्ठे विदर्भेषु) 12. 264. 3. C. Epic events: (1) On the second day of war, Vidarbha warriors and others along with their armies accompanied Droṇa who was behind Bhīṣma in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas (विदर्भैर् मेकलैश् चैव … सहिताः सर्वसैन्येन) 6. 47. 10, 12-13. D. Past events: (a) from the story of Nala: (1) King Bhīma once ruled over the Vidarbha country 3. 50. 5; 3. 61. 72; he protected it well (सम्यग् गोप्ता विदर्भाणां … ) 3. 61. 44; (2) The swans promised Nala that they would praise him in the presence of Damayantī, flew towards Vidharbha and reached its principal town (विदर्भ-नगरीं गत्वा) 3. 50. 21-22; (3) The guardians of the world, Indra and others, started for the Vidarbha country to attend the स्वयंवर of Damayantī 3. 51. 24; (4) As directed by Damayantī, Vārṣṇeya, the charioteer of Nala, put her two children (son and a daughter) on a chariot and took them to her father in Vidarbha (ययौ मिथुनम् आरोप्य विदर्भांस् तेन वाहिना) 3. 57. 20 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 60. 19: मिथुनं कुमारं कुमारीं च): (5) Nala pointed out to Damayantī the road that led to the Vidarbha country; she asked him why he showed to her the road to Vidarbha; she suggested to him that both of them together, and not she alone, might go to Vidarbha 3. 58. 22, 30, 33; (6) When Sudeva saw Damayantī in the Cedi country, he thought her to be like a lotus plant lifted from a pond of the Vidarbha country (विदर्भसरसस् तस्माद् दैव-दोषाद् इवोद्धृताम् । … मृणालीम् इव) 3. 65. 12; (7) Damayantī told the mother of Subāhu, the king of Cedis, that she wished to go to Vidarbha; she was accordingly sent to Vidarbha 3. 66. 19, 22; (8) King Ṛtuparṇa told Bāhuka (Nala) that he wished to go to Vidarbha in a day to attend Damayantī's स्वयंवर (विदर्भान् यातुम् इच्छामि … । एकाह्ना); Bāhuka assured him that he would be able to reach the capital town of Vidarbha in a day although the horses he (Bāhuka) had chosen were lean (प्रतिजानामि ते सत्यं गमिष्यसि … । एकाह्ना … विदर्भनगरीं नृप ॥ ) 3. 69. 2, 9, 15; on way, Ṛtuparṇa, although he relied on Bāhuka to reach Vidarbha on time, told him not to raise any obstacle; if Bāhuka took him to Vidarbha before sunset he would give Bāhuka anything he wanted (विदर्भान् यदि यात्वाद्य सूर्यं दर्श-यितासि मे । कामं च ते करीष्यामि); but Bāhuka told Ṛtuparṇa that he would first count the Vibhītaka fruit and then proceed to Vidarbha; when Kali had left Nala's body, king Ṛtuparṇa proceeded to Vidarbha 3. 70. 17-19, 38; Ṛtuparṇa reached Vidarbha in the evening (विदर्भान् संप्राप्तं सायाह्ने) 3. 71. 1; (b) other past event: Once a certain Brāhmaṇa lived in the Vida-rbha country (विदर्भेष्व् अभवद् द्विजः) 12. 264. 3. E. Some persons referred to with reference to the Vidarbha country as the king of Vidarbha, one belonging to Vidarbha, etc.: A. King of Vidarbha; (a) विदर्भपति: Bhīma 3. 51. 5; (b) विदर्भराज्: Bhīma 3. 61. 119; (c) विदर्भराज: (1) Bhīma 3. 66. 1; (विद-र्भराजदुहिता) 3. 51. 19; 3. 58. 34; (विद-र्भराजतनया) 3. 61. 31; (2) A king, not named, father of Lopāmudrā 3. 94. 18; (3) A king, neither named or identified 3. 120. 30; (d) विदर्भाधिप: Bhīma 3. 61. 8 (विदर्भाधिपनन्दिनी); (e) विदर्भाधि-पति: Bhīma 3. 61. 41; 3. 67. 7; (f) Pro-tector of Vidarbhas: Bhīma गोप्ता विदर्-भाणाम् 3. 61. 44; B. Daughter of Vidarbha: Damayantī: विदर्भतनया 3. 61. 11; C. One belonging to Vidarbha: (a) वैदर्भ: A king, not named, father of Lopāmudrā 3. 94. 20; 3. 95. 1; (b) वैदर्भी (f.): (1) Damayantī 3. 52. 11, 21; 3. 53. 5, 12; 3. 54. 11, 13; 3. 56. 8; 3. 59. 5, 17; 3. 61. 55; 3. 62. 12; 3. 64. 9; 3. 65. 6, 23, 27; 3. 68. 17; 3. 69. 5; 3. 71. 31; 3. 72. 7, 21-22; 3. 74. 5; 3. 75. 22; 3. 76. 1; 3. 77. 20; (2) Maryādā, wife of Arācīna 1. 90. 18; (3) Lopāmudrā 3. 94. 27; 5. 115. 12; (4) Suṣuvā, wife of Jayat-sena 1. 90. 17; (5) Wife of Sagara, not named 3. 104. 8, 7; D. The principal town Kuṇḍina of Vidarbha referred to as विदर्भनगरी 3. 50. 22; 3. 69. 9.
विदेह: Videha1 m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada and its people; once named (perhaps for metre) Videhaka 6. 10. 44. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (विदेहका मागधाश् च) 6. 10. 44 (here Videhakas are listed along with Māgadhas as apposed to Videhas2 listed by Saṃjaya along with Kirātas, Barbaras and others); the Janapada lay in the east beyond Pāñ-cālas and the river Gaṇḍakī 2. 26. 3-4 (see Epic event No. 2 below); Vātikaṣaṇḍa (?) lay to the north of Videhas (एष वातिक-षण्डो वै … विदेहान् उत्तरं च यः) 3. 130. 13; Videhas lived in Mithilā (see Epic event No. 1 below) 1. 105. 11. B. Description of its warriors and people: Strong (बलवन्त्) 6. 112. 107; great chariot-fighters (महारथ) 6. 112. 107, 111; very difficult to be conquered in battle (संख्ये सुदुर्जयाः) 8. 57. 31; the Videha country was inhabited by very prosperous people (समृद्धजनसेवित) 12. 312. 22. C. Epic events: (1) In Pāṇḍu's conquest of the earth which he undertook after his marriage, he went to Mithilā and defeated Videhas in battle (जिगीषमाणो वसुधां … पाण्डुना मिथिलां गत्वा विदेहाः समरे जिताः) 1. 105. 7, 11; (2) Bhīmasena, in his expedition to the east (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1; 2. 23. 9) went beyond Pāñcālas and the river Gaṇḍakī and defeat-ed Videhas 2. 26. 3-4; (3) On the tenth day of the war, Videha warriors (on the side of Kauravas) as directed by Duryo-dhana who assured them the protection of Bhīṣma, attacked Arjuna; Arjuna burnt them and their armies with his heavenly missiles (दिव्यान्य् अस्त्राणि संचिन्त्य प्र-संधाय); afflicted by arrows and with their chariots and banners broken they did not attack Arjuna (शरार्ता … विप्रकीर्णरथध्वजाः । … नाभ्यवर्तन्त  … वानरध्वजम्) 6. 112. 102, 105, 108, 110-112, 114; on the same day, in the meeting between Bhīṣma and Karṇa after the former's downfall, Bhīṣma reminded Karṇa in order to encourage him that he had formerly defeated Videhas (7. 4. 5); on the seventeenth day, Śalya too, in order to encourage Karṇa reminded him that he had once with great courage defeated Videhas (वैदेहा° … यया धृत्या जिताः सं-ख्ये सुदुर्जयाः) 8. 57. 31; later Dhṛta-rāṣṭra while lamenting over the death of Karṇa remembered that Karṇa had defeated Videhas and made them pay tribute (विदे-हांश् च … । यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा ॥ ) 8. 5. 19-20 (reference in all three cases to Karṇa's दिग्विजय before the Vaiṣṇavayajña of Duryodhana 3. 241. 29, 32; 3. App. 24-42 (मिथिलान्)); (4) On the seventeenth day, at night (निशि 8. 1. 25), Saṃjaya in his first brief account of the death of Karṇa, mentioned that Karṇa killed many Videhas (on the side of Pāṇḍavas) in the presence of all Sṛñjayas and Pāñcālas (स सृञ्जयानां सर्वेषां पाञ्चालानां च पश्यताम् … विदेहानाम् अकरोत् कदनं महत् ॥ ) 8. 2. 18. D. Past events: (1) King Janaka gave his son the kingdom of Videha and himself lived the life of a mendicant (विदेहराज्यं तथा प्रतिष्ठाप्य सुतस्य वै) 12. 306. 94; (2) Sulabhā went to the capital town of Videhas (विदेहानां पुरीं … ) 12. 308. 11; (3) Śuka, as instructed by Vyāsa, reached the country of Videhas which was protected by Janaka (विदेहान् आससाद ह । रक्षितान् धर्मराजेन जनकेन) 12. 312. 6, 19; Śuka entered the country of Videhas and reached the garden in Mithilā (स विदेहान् अतिक्रम्य … मिथि-लोपवनं रम्यं आससाद) 12. 312. 22. E. Some kings referred to as: A. the king of Videhas: (a) विदेहराज: (1) Janaka, father of Sītā 3. 132. 4; 3. 258. 9; (2) Janaka, the philosopher 12. 18. 3; 12. 28. 57; 12. 171. 55; 12. 268. 3; 12. 286. 41; 12. 313. 10; 13. 45. 7; (3) Hayagrīva 5. 72. 15; (4) A king, not named 13. 46. 11 (विदेहराजदुहिता); (b) विदेहराजन्; Janaka, the philosopher 12. 18. 2; B. some kings and princesses referred to as belong-ing to Videha: (a) वैदेह: (1) Karāla-janaka 12. 296. 37 (cf. 12. 291. 7-8); (2) Janaka, the philosopher 12. 28. 3; 12. 285. 16; 12. 286. 17; 12. 307. 4, 6; (3) Nimi 12. 226. 26; (4) A king, not named 12. 106. 6; 12. 107. 8. 9, 26; (5) A king, not named, contemporary of Pāṇḍavas 2. 4. 24 (cf. the next वैदेहक); (b) वैदेहक: Janaka, contemporary of Pāṇḍavas, who was con-quered by Bhīma 2. 27. 12 (cf. वैदेह (5) above); (c) वैदेही (f.): (1) Maryādā 1. 90. 22; (2) Sītā, daughter of Janaka 3. 261. 28; 3. 262. 17, 23; 3. 263. 7, 10-11, 13-14, 23, 28-29; 3. 264. 5, 14, 53, 71; 3. 265. 17-18, 30; 3. 266. 23, 35, 55, 66; 3. 273. 26; 3. 275. 102, 21, 56, 63; 3. 276. 10; 4. 20. 9; (3) A princess, not named, married to Śatānīka 1. 90. 95.

Videha2 m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (किराता बर्बराः सिद्धा विदेहास् ताम्रलिङ्ग-काः) 6. 10. 55 (these Videhas seem to be different from Videhas1 since these are listed along with Kirātas and others). B. Description: Karṇa mentioned to Śalya of a certain Brāhmaṇa who in the Kuru assembly, equated Videhas with Āraṭṭas (Bāhlīkas) and described them as non-sacrificers, those who had lost their धर्म and hence whose country should not be visited; this description seems to apply to these Videhas2 and not to Videha1 above (आरट्टा नाम ते देशा नष्टधर्मान् न तान् व्रजेत् । व्रात्यानां दासमी यानां विदेहानाम् अयज्वनाम्) 8. 30. 36.
विन्ध्यपुलक: Vindhyapulaka m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा … ) 6. 10. 56, 5; (तथैव विन्ध्य-पुलकाः पुलिन्दाः … ) 6. 10. 60.
वीरक: Vīraka m. (pl.): Name of a people. According to a Brāhmaṇa reporting to the Kuru assembly, a certain Rākṣasī described Vīrakas as those who followed bad धर्म and therefore should be com-pletely avoided (कर्कोटकान् वीरकांश् च दुर्धर्मांश् च विवर्जयेत्) 8. 30. 41, 45-46.
वृष्णि: Vṛṣṇi m. (pl.): Name of a people, occasionally referred to as Vārṣṇeyas; often mentioned along with Andhakas and some-times also with Bhojas. A. Location: They lived in the city Dvārakā; the city is referred to as वृष्णिपुर 3. 21. 4; 3. 180. 25; वृष्ण्यन्धकपुर 3. 16. 19 (see below Epic events No. 17). B. Origin: The origin of the Vṛṣṇi race is sought in the extensive race of Prajāpati known as the progeny of Śaśabindu (प्रजाम् आचक्षते विप्राः पौराणीं शाशबिन्दवीम् । स वृष्णिवंशप्रभवो महावंशः प्रजा-पतेः ॥ ) 12. 201. 13 (Comm. Arjunamiśra on 12. 201. 11: शशबिन्दुः वृष्णीनां पूर्वजः । सो ऽपि प्रजापतिः); see Editor's note, Cr. edn. Vol. 16, p. 2166). C. Greatness: While narrating the descent of the first generations (आदिवंशावतार), Vaiśaṃpāyana told Janamejaya that the all-pervading Puruṣa took birth (as Kṛṣṇa) among the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas for fur-thering the cause of धर्म (पुरुषः स विभुः … । धर्मसंवर्धनार्थाय प्र-जज्ञे ऽन्धकवृष्णिषु) 1. 57. 87; Nārāyaṇa was born as Kṛṣṇa in the family of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas 2. 33. 17; 2. 34. 15. D. Description and characteristics: Of good nature (सुमनस्) 5. 84. 4; very fortunate (सुमहाभाग) 12. 82. 8; having all enjoy-ments (भोगवन्त्) 5. 28. 12; prosperous (स्फीत) 5. 84. 3; prosperous because they were always active (नित्योत्थानेन सं-पन्नाः) 12. 82. 8; magnanimous (महात्-मन्) 1. 213. 53; 3. 119. 2; 16. 9. 26; of great lustre (सुमहौजस्) 1. 211. 5; spirited (मनस्विन्) 5. 28. 12; brave (शूर) and proud like lion (सिंहदर्प) 16. 9. 9; heroic (वीर, वीर्यवन्त्) 2. 13. 59; excellent heroes (उत्तमवीर्य) 1. 213. 55: strong, very strong (बलिन्) 2. 17. 27; (महाबल) 2. 13. 59; 5. 28 12; 16. 9. 9; (बलवन्त्) 12. 82. 8; powerful (सामर्थ्य-वन्त्) 2. 13. 53; great archers (महेष्वास) 2. 72. 29; 3. 48. 6; tigers among men (पुरुषव्याघ्र) 1. 212. 14; immensely powerful like tigers (व्याघ्रैर् इव बलो-त्कटैः) 5. 154. 17; proficient in all शास्त्रस् (सर्वशास्त्रविशारद) 3. 119. 2; difficult to be attacked (दुर्धर्ष) 2. 4. 26; (दुरासद) 12. 82. 8; of ture valour (सत्यपराक्रम) 5. 28. 12; bringing toge-ther people (?) (लोकसंहनन) 2. 13. 59; having long arms, like iron bars (बाहुशालिन्, परिघबाहु) 16. 9. 10-11; their arms were capable of resisting maces, iron bars and शक्तिस् (गदापरिघशक्तीनां सहाः) 16. 9. 10; they were like Indra (इन्द्रकल्प) 5. 28. 12; like gods (देवरूपिन्) 2. 4. 26; attached to Kṛṣṇa (त्वय्य् आसक्ताः) 12. 82. 29; Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas followed the advice of Kṛṣṇa (यस्य प्रज्ञाम् उपासते) 5. 84. 4; following Kṛṣṇa's advice, Vārṣṇe-yas and Bhojas restrained their enemies and gave delight to friends (वार्ष्णेयभोजाः  … उपासीना वासुदेवस्य बुद्धिं निगृह्य शत्रून् सुहृदो नन्दयन्ति) 5. 28. 11; no one in the past was or in the future would be equal to Vṛṣṇis in strength; they did not disregard kinsmen, were obedient to elders, gods, Asuras, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣa-sas; men were unable to defeat Vṛṣṇi warriors in battles: they did not rob Brāh-maṇas, teachers, kinsmen of their wealth; on the other hand, if any one of them was in difficulty they protected him; they were wealthy, but were not arrogant; truthful, they were devoted to Brāhmaṇas; they did not underrate the strong ones, they uplifted the weak ones; they worshipped gods, were controlled and generous, but not given to boasting; due to these virtues Vṛṣṇi warriors were not attacked; one might carry moun-tain Meru, cross the ocean, but not succeed if he dared attack Vṛṣṇi warriors (न तुल्यं … भूतं भव्यं भविष्यच् च बलेन; समर्थान् नावमन्यन्ते दीनान् अभ्युद्धरन्ति च; तेन वृष्णिप्रवीराणां चक्रं न प्रतिहन्यते; Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 144. 28: चक्रं प्रतापः 7. 119. 22-27 (this description of Vṛṣṇis immediately follows that of the Sātvatas (7. 119. 20-21) which is indicative of the identity between the two); Bhūriśravas deriding Sātyaki ridiculed Vṛṣṇis as व्रात्यस्, not distin-guishing between good and evil acts, and despicable by very nature (व्रात्याः सं-श्लिष्तकर्माणः प्रकृत्यैव विगर्हिताः) 7. 118. 15. E. Epic events: (1) The Vṛṣṇis went to the forest to meet Pāṇḍavas (वृष्णीनाम् आगमो यत्र)—a reference to a later epic event (see No. 15 below) in the summary of the contents of the Āraṇyaka-parvan (given in the sub-parvan पर्वसं-ग्रह) 1. 2. 106; (2) Yudhiṣṭhira heard from Nārada the massive mutual destruc-tion of the Vṛṣṇis—a reference to a later event (see below No. 65) in the summary of the contents of the Āśramavāsikaparvan 1. 2. 217 (actually this event does not form part of the Āśramavāsikaparvan but of the Mausalaparvan and Yudhiṣṭhira did not get the news from Nārada but from Dāruka (cf. 16. 1. 7; 16. 6. 11); Arjuna seeing Dvārakā without Vṛṣṇis was dejected 1. 2. 223; he performed the funeral rites of Rāma, Kṛṣṇa and other Vṛṣṇi-chiefs (वृष्णीनां च प्रधानतः); he felt sad on account of the abduction of Vṛṣṇi women (नाशं वृष्णिकलत्राणाम्) 1. 2. 227—all three events are references given in the summary of the Mausalaparvan to later epic events (see below Epic events Nos. 70-75); (3) Vṛṣṇis learnt the science of archery (धनुर्वेद) from Kṛpa 1. 120. 21; Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas approached Droṇa to learn the अस्त्रस् (अस्त्रार्थे … वृष्णयश् चान्धकाश् चैव) 1. 122. 46; (4) Vṛṣṇi chiefs attend-ed the स्वयंवर of Draupadī 1. 177. 18; as advised by Kṛṣṇa they watched the pro-ceedings of the स्वयंवर 1. 178. 8; (5) Bhoja, Vṛṣṇi, and Andhaka women gathered to see Arjuna when he arrived at Dvārakā; Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas honoured and greeted Arjuna; he paid his respects to the deserving among them; Vṛṣṇis, along with Bhojas and Andhakas celebrated a grand festival in honour of the Raivataka mountain; in that festival, Vṛṣṇis and others gave gifts to thousands of Brāhmaṇas; thousands of illustrious youths of Vṛṣṇis put on ornaments and moved about riding vehicles decorated with gold; their wives and followers accompani-ed them 1. 211. 1-2, 5-6; (6) On hearing the sound of the drum sounded by the guardian of the Sabhā, agitated Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, leaving aside food and drink, assembled by hundreds in the Sabhā and took their seats on the सिंहासनस्; the Sabhāpāla told them that Arjuna had ab-ducted Subhadrā; on hearing it they leaped up from their seats and asked their chari-oteers to yoke the chariots and bring their weapons, bows and armours; others brought forth their gold-decked horses; when all these arrangements were being done there arose a confused sound of the Vṛṣṇi heroes 1. 212. 12-19; Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas got ready to follow Balarāma when he announced his intention to fight with Arjuna (अन्वपद्यन्त ते सर्वे भोज-वृष्ण्यन्धकास् तदा) 1. 212. 31-32; Vṛṣṇis made their intention to attack Arjuna known several times; but when Kṛṣṇa told them that Arjuna had done the right thing, they were pacified 1. 213. 2-11; Kṛṣṇa with Vṛṣṇis and others went to the Khāṇḍava-prastha to attend the marriage of Subhadrā with Arjuna; they took with them large number of nuptial gifts (हरणं बहु); they were received by Nakula and Saha-deva; the illustrious Vṛṣṇis (वृष्णिचक्रं समृद्धिमत्) entered Khāṇḍavaprastha; Yudhiṣṭhira received the seniors among Vṛṣṇis with honours according to the rules and following the actual practice (?) (प्रति-जग्राह सत्कारैर् यथाविधि यथोपगम्); he honoured some Vṛṣṇi-chiefs as elders, some as friends; he greeted some with affection and was himself greeted by some (गुरुवत् पूजयाम् आस कांश्चित् कांश्चिद् वयस्यवत् । कांश्चिद् अभ्यवदत् प्रेम्णा कैश् चिद् अप्य् अभिवादितः ॥ ) 1. 213. 23-24, 29, 31, 34, 38-39; after receiving their gifts, Yudhiṣṭhira honoured the great warriors of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas (वृष्ण्य्-अन्धकमहारथान्); the best among the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas (वृष्ण्यन्धकोत्त-माः) lived happily with Kurus and enjoyed with them great drinking bouts (महा-पानैर् … विजह्रुः कुरुवृष्णयः); then, after many days, the Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka warriors (उत्तमवीर्यास् ते), led by Bala-rāma, returned to Dvārakā taking with them bright jewels given to them by Kurus 1. 213. 52-56; (7) Vṛṣṇi princes (वृष्णीनां … कुमारा … ) were among those who waited on Dharmarāja in his Sabhā 2. 4. 26; (8) They were taught the science of archery by Arjuna (कुमारा … वृष्णि-नन्दनाः) 2. 4. 29; (9) Vṛṣṇis fled from Mathurā and settled down at Kuśa-sthalī in the west; they fortified the new settlement in such a way as to make it difficult to be captured even by gods; even women could fight and hold it against the attack (स्त्रियो ऽपि यस्यां युध्येयुः किं पुनर् वृष्णिपुंगवाः 2. 13. 51); Vṛṣṇis lived there without fear from any quarter (अकुतोभयाः); although powerful, they had allied themselves with Pāṇḍavas because of their relationship (सामर्थ्य-वन्तः सम्बन्धाद् भवन्तं समुपा-श्रिताः); Cārudeṣṇa and all other Vṛṣṇi heroes though free from grief, lived at Kuśasthalī still remembering the Madhya-deśa (where they formerly lived) (स्मरन्तो मध्यमं देशं वृष्णिमध्ये गत-व्यथाः) 2. 13. 53, 59; (10) Jarāsandha was neglected by Vṛṣṇis, though strong, out of considerations of policy (बलिभिः  … वृष्णिभिश् च … नीतिहेतोर् उपेक्षितः) 2. 17. 27; (11) Vṛṣṇis arrived at Khāṇḍava-prastha for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira 2. 31. 16; (12) Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas did not pay tribute to Yudhiṣṭhira for Rājasūya because of their friendly relations with Pāṇḍavas (सख्येनान्धकवृष्णयः) 2. 48. 42; however, Vārṣṇeyas are said to have brought for Yudhiṣṭhira many kinds of tribute (वार्ष्णेयान् हारहूणांश् च  … बल्यर्थं ददतस् तस्मै नानारूपान् अनेकशः) but were stopped at the gate 2. 47. 19-20, 25; the tribute is described in 2. 47. 21-25 (since Vārṣṇeyas are here listed along with Cīnas, Hūṇas, Śakas, Oḍras, forest-dwellers, and Hārahūṇas, are these Vārṣṇeyas different from Vṛṣṇis who formed a section of the Yādavas and did not pay tribute ?): (13) Śiśupāla instigated the kings assembled for the Rājasūya to fight with Vṛṣṇis and Pāṇḍavas 2. 36. 14; (14) Vidura warned Kauravas that Vṛṣṇis would never forgive the hardship suffered by Drau-padī in the Sabhā (तस्याः … परिक्लेशं न क्षंस्यन्ते … । वृष्णयो वा महेष्वासाः) 2. 72. 29; (15) Hearing that Pāṇḍavas had gone into exile, Vṛṣṇis, Bhojas, and Andhakas went to meet them in the Dvaitavana (3. 12. 68); they sat around Yudhiṣṭhira, blamed Kauravas and won-dered what they could do (to help them) 3. 13. 1, 3-4; (16) Draupadī complained to Kṛṣṇa that Kauravas had desired to reduce her to the status of a दासी although Vṛṣṇis were alive (दासीभावेन भोक्तुं माम् ईषुस् ते मधुसूदन । जीवत्सु … अथ वृष्णिषु) 3. 13. 56; 5. 80. 25; (17) When Śālva attacked Dvārakā in the absence of Kṛṣṇa, young Vṛṣṇi heroes fought with him (बालकैर् वृष्णिपुंगवैः); Śālva killed many of the excellent Vṛṣṇi heroes (वृष्णि-प्रवीरांस् तान् बालान् हत्वा) 3. 15. 6-7; during Śālva's attack on Dvārakā drinking liquor was prohibited; Vṛṣṇis and Andha-kas had to remain alert apprehending Śālva might attack them when they were drunk (प्रमत्तेष्व् अभिघातं हि कुर्यात्  … इति कृत्वाप्रमत्तास् ते सर्वे वृष्ण्य्-अन्धकाः स्थिताः ॥ ) 3. 16. 12-13; it was then ruled that no one in the town of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas could leave or enter the town without valid permit (न चामुद्रो ऽभिनिर्याति न चामुद्रः प्रवेश्यते । वृष्ण्य-न्धकपुरे) 3. 16. 19; when the youthful Vṛṣṇi princes saw Śālva's army attacking Dvārakā, they came out and fought with the opponents (कुमारा वृष्णिनन्दनाः) 3. 17. 8; when Pradyumna swooned, the army of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas raised a cry of grief; when Pradyumna regained consciousness he blamed his charioteer for removing his chariot away from the battle-field for that was not the battle-धर्म of Vṛṣṇ warriors (नैष वृष्णिप्रवीराणाम् आहवे धर्म उच्यते) 3. 19. 1-2, 5; he told the charioteer that one who left the battlefield was not born in the family of Vṛṣṇis (न स वृष्णिकुले जातो यो वै त्यजति संगरम्), nor he who killed one fallen on the ground or who had surrendered, or a woman, an old man or a child, or one who was without a chariot, who was shattered, and whose weapons were broken; he reminded the charioteer that he (the charioteer) knew what the धर्म of Vṛṣṇis was in battles, and since he knew the entire code of conduct of Vṛṣṇis en-gaged in fighting he should not have taken Pradyumna away form battlefield; (धर्-मज्ञश् चासि वृष्णीनाम् आहवेष्व् अपि … । स जानंश् चरितं कृत्स्नं वृष्णीणां पृतना-मुखे । ) 3. 19. 13-16; Pradyumna wonder-ed what the women of Vṛṣṇi heroes would say to him when he met them 3. 19. 21; Pradyumna asked his charioteer how he could face Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis who always vied with him (मया स्पर्धन्ति सततं) 3. 19. 28; the charioteer in reply told Pradyumna that he was conversant with the war (conduct) of Vṛṣṇis (and he defended his action) (युद्धज्ञश् चास्मि वृष्णीनाम्) 3. 20. 2; Śālva tormented by Vṛṣṇis rode his Saubha to rise up in the sky and left Dvārakā 3. 20. 27; when Kṛṣṇa returned to Dvārakā he was sur-prised to see the town of Vṛṣṇis with men and women extremely uneasy (अस्वस्थ-नरनारीकम् इदं वृष्णिपुरं भृशम्) 3. 21. 4; Kṛṣṇa then spoke to Āhuka, Vasu-deva and Vṛṣṇi heroes asking them to remain alert (अप्रमादः सदा कार्यो); he announced his decision to attack Śālva which delighted Vṛṣṇis; comforted, they asked him to kill the enemies and blessed him 3. 21. 7-11; (18) Dhṛtarāṣṭra feared that Vṛṣṇi archers and spirited Pāñcālas, led by Kṛṣṇa, would burn the army of Kauravas 3. 48. 6; he told Saṃjaya that it was not possible even for mountains to withstand the velocity (of the attack) of Vṛṣṇis when led by Rāma and Kṛṣṇa (वृष्णीनाम् … । न शक्यः सहितुं वेगः) 3. 48. 7; (19) When Vṛṣṇis went to Prabhāsa to meet the Pāṇḍavas during the period of their exile, they found them smeared with dirt resting on bare ground; seeing them, Vṛṣṇis were filled with sorrow and cried loudly; Yudhiṣṭhira approached Vṛṣṇis and honoured them as they deserved; they too in return honoured Pāṇḍavas and sat around them 3. 118. 15, 18-21; Janamejaya asked Vaiśaṃpāyana to tell him the details of the talks between Vṛṣṇis, sitting around, and Pāṇḍavas at Prabhāsa 3. 119. 1-3; Sātyaki suggested to Balarāma that he should permit the army of Daśārhas to march against Duryodhana so that he would perish when overtaken by the army of Vṛṣṇis; he also said that the army consisting of principal Kṣatriya warriors of Vṛṣṇis, Bhojas and Andhakas should kill the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and enhance its fame (क्षत्रियशूरसेना लोके यशः स्फीतम् उपाकरोतु) 3. 120. 5, 19; (20) Kṛṣṇa told Draupadī that her sons while they were in the town of Vṛṣṇis (Dvārakā) they were not jealous of gods (तवात्मजा वृष्णिपुरं प्रविश्य न दैवतेभ्यः स्पृहयन्ति कृष्णे) 3. 180. 25; Satyabhāmā assured Draupadī that Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis had the same affec-tion for her sons as for Pradyumna 3. 224. 14; (21) Draupadī warned Jayadratha that if he insisted on abducting her, Vṛṣṇi heroes led by Kṛṣṇa, would chase him (वृष्णिवीरा … पदवीं चरेयुः) 3. 252. 16 (Nī. on 3. 268. 14 (in another context) पदवीं चरेतां अन्वेषणं कुरुतः); (22) Vṛṣṇis, Bhojas and Andhakas went to Upaplavya to attend the marriage of Abhimanyu 4. 67. 14, 24; Vṛṣṇis, Andhakas and Bhojas returned to Dvārakā after the marriage 5. 7. 1; (23) Saṃjaya advised Yudhiṣṭhira that it was more beneficial for him to live by begging in the kingdom of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas than get back the kingdom by resorting to war (भैक्ष्य-चर्यां अन्धकवृष्णिराज्ये श्रेयो मन्ये न तु युद्धेन राज्यम्) 5. 27. 2; (24) An-dhakas, Vārṣṇeyas and Bhojas followed the advice of Kṛṣṇa and therefore they could restrain the enemies and delight their friends (अन्धकाश् च वार्ष्णेयभोजाः); Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, led by Kṛṣṇa, were like Indra (कृष्णप्रणीताः सर्व एवेन्द्र-कल्पाः) 5. 28. 11-12; (25) The son of Ugrasena (Kaṃsa) once shone amongst Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas (वृष्ण्यन्धकानां मध्यगतं तपन्तम्) 5. 47. 72; (26) Once Nārada advised Vṛṣṇis that they should do their duty (तस्मात् कर्मैव कर्तव्यम् इति होवाच नारदः । … वृष्णि-चक्रस्य) 5. 48. 22 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 5. 49. 22: कर्म युद्धं कर्तव्यं तयोर् (i. e. कृष्णार्जुनयोः) इति शेषः । आचष्ट आख्यातवान् नारद एव); (27) Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas could not be subjugated by Jarāsandha either due to the policy adopted by them or due to sheer luck (नयेनान्धकवृष्णयः । ते न तस्य वशं जग्मुः केवलं दैवम् एव वा) 5. 50. 39; (28) Kṛṣṇa protected Vṛṣṇis in all calamities (सर्वास्व् आपत्सु) 5. 70. 4; (29) According to Duryodhana if Kṛṣṇa was arrested Vṛṣṇis would be under his control (तस्मिन् बद्धे भवि-ष्यन्ति वृष्णयः … विधेया मे) 5. 86. 14; (30) When Kṛṣṇa mounted the chariot to go to the Sabhā of Kauravas he was pro-tected by Vṛṣṇis whose great chariot-fighters followed him (पृष्ठतो ऽनुययुः); when he entered the Sabhā they walked behind him (आसन् कृष्णस्य पृष्ठतः) 5. 92. 14, 17, 33; (31) All Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis lived happily together when the Yādavas abandoned Kaṃsa in the interest of the family (संभूय सुखं एधन्ते) 5. 126. 39; (32) Kṛṣṇa told Duryodhana that he was not alone in the Sabhā; Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis were with him; and when he laughed to show the great miracle (महद् आश्चर्यं 5. 129. 14) Vṛṣṇis and others, ready with weapons (समुद्यतमहा-युधाः), were there in front of him 5. 129. 3, 8-9; (33) Kṛṣṇa asked Karṇa to recognize Vṛṣṇis who were his kin from the mother's side (viz. Kuntī) (मातृपक्षे च वृष्णयः । द्वौ पक्षाव् अभिजानीहि); in that case Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis would follow him 5. 138. 10, 13, 23; (34) Yudhi-ṣṭhira settled down in his camp at Kuru-kṣetra along with Vṛṣṇis (वृष्निभिश् चैव  … वृतम्) 5. 150. 2; (35) Balarāma came to Pāṇḍavas along with Vṛṣṇi chiefs (वृष्णि-मुख्यैर् अभिगतैः) 5. 154. 17; but he decided not to take part in the war from any side and left for pilgrimage along with Vṛṣṇis 9. 34. 1, 5, 12; (cf. 5. 154. 34); (36) Before the start of the war in the camp of Kauravas, Bṛhadbala along with the great warriors of Andhakas, Vṛṣṇis and Bhojas stood guard on the right side of the army (बलं त्वदीयं दक्षिणतो ऽभिपाति) 6. 20. 14; (37) On the ninth day of the war, at night, Pāṇḍavas sat down to take counsel with Vṛṣṇis (वृष्णि-भिः सह । … मन्त्राय समुपाविशन्) 6. 103. 10; (38) In the estimate of Vṛṣṇis, Cekitāna was a match for a hundred warriors in battle (शताद् विशिष्टं यं युद्धे समपश्यन्त वृष्णयः) 7. 9. 50; (39) Droṇa, in order to encourage Jaya-dratha said that, after all, Vṛṣṇis and the rest were not eternal and that some day they (and by turn they all) were going to die (वृष्णयो ऽन्ये च मानवाः । … अध्रुवा  … । … पर्यायेण वयं सर्वे … परलोकं गमिष्यामः) 7. 52. 30-31; (40) Subhadrā wondered who could have killed Abhi-manyu when Vṛṣṇi heroes were there to protect him; she pitied the heroism of Vṛṣṇi warriors (नाथेषु … वृष्णिवीरेषु; धिग् वीर्यं वृष्णिवीराणाम्) 7. 55. 9, 12; (41) On the fourteenth day, Saṃjaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that Pāṇḍavas, Vṛṣṇis and others would blame him for the confusion in his mind (ते बुद्धिव्यभीचारम् उप-लप्स्यन्ति) 7. 62. 7; the same day, Yudhi-ṣṭhira remembered that Arjuna, to praise Sātyaki, had told him in Dvaitavana that he would need Sātyaki's help even though Vṛṣṇis, led by Kṛṣṇa, were ready to help him 7. 85. 54, 58-60; Bhūriśravas wondered how Arjuna could look upon Vṛṣṇis and Andha-kas who, by very nature were despicable, as authority (while deciding what was proper or improper in war) (प्रकृत्यैव विगर्-हिताः । वृष्ण्यन्धकाः कथं पार्थ प्र-माणं भवता कृताः ॥ ) 7. 118. 15; (42) During the night war (14th-15th day), Karṇa assured Duryodhana that he would defeat Vṛṣṇis and the rest 7. 133. 11; after the death of Droṇa, Sātyaki told Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna that he deserved to be expelled (from the war) by Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis since he did a vile act and yet praised himself (याप्यस् त्वम् असि … सर्वैश् चाप्य्-अन्धकवृष्णिभिः) 7. 169. 11; (43) Saha-deva told Sātyaki that just as Pāṇḍavas had no friends other than Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, they too had no friends other than Pāṇḍavas 7. 169. 48-49; Pāñcālas too had no friends better than Pāṇḍavas and Vṛṣṇis 7. 169. 50; (44) On the fifteenth day, when the Pāṇḍava army was being burnt by the Nārāyaṇāstra, Yudhiṣṭhira advised Sātyaki to leave the battle-field along with Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas 7. 170. 26; (45) On the seventeenth day, at night (निशि 8. 1. 25), Dhṛtarāṣṭra while lamenting the death of Karṇa, told Saṃjaya that Karṇa, depending on the strength of his arms, never thought highly of Vṛṣṇis (नामन्यत वै नित्यम् … न वृष्णीन् अपि … स्वबाहुबलम् आश्रितः ॥ ) 8. 5. 15; (46) After the fall of Duryodhana, when Bala-rāma, in anger, left for Dvārakā, Pāñcālas and Vārṣṇeyas were disheartened (पाञ्चालाश् च सवार्ष्णेयाः … नातिप्रमनसो ऽभवन्) 9. 59. 27; (47) Kṛṣṇa narrated to Yudhi-ṣṭhira that Aśvatthāman had once come to Dvārakā where he was highly honoured by Vṛṣṇis (वृष्णिभिः परमार्चितः) 10. 12. 11; Kṛṣṇa told Aśvatthāman that he was never before requested to part with his चक्र by any one of the great warriors among Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas (as Aśvatthāman did) 10. 12. 33; (48) Kṛṣṇa told Gāndhārī that there was no one else except himself who could extirpate the clan of Vṛṣṇis (सं-हर्ता वृष्णिचक्रस्य) 11. 25. 44; (49) While repenting the loss of life in war, Yudhiṣṭhira said to Arjuna that if Pāṇḍa-vas, instead of waging war, had chosen to beg in the town of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas they would not have killed the males in the army of their kinsmen and would not have met with the misfortune (यद् भैक्षम् आचरिष्याम वृष्ण्यन्धकपुरे वयम् । ज्ञातीन् निष्पुरुषान् कृत्वा नेमां प्राप्स्याम दुर्गतिन्) 12. 7. 3; (50) Yudhiṣṭhira while addressing Vyāsa pitied the plight of war widows who would curse Pāṇḍavas along with Vṛṣṇis 12. 33. 8; (51) Kṛṣṇa told Arjuna that a very long time had elapsed since he was with Baladeva and other Vṛṣṇi chiefs in Dvārakā (वृष्णिपुंगवान्) and he would therefore like to return to Dvārakā 14. 15. 20; Arjuna assured him that he would soon meet them; Yudhiṣṭhira re-quested Kṛṣṇa to return to Hāstinapura for the Aśvamedha after meeting Vṛṣṇis 14. 51. 23, 46; (52) When Kṛṣṇa returned to Dvārakā, Vṛṣṇi heroes were celebrating the festival of the Raivataka mountain (विहारो वृष्णिवीराणाम् महे रैवतकस्य ह) 14. 58. 13; Bhojas, Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis received Kṛṣṇa on the Raivataka; Kṛṣṇa honoured them and enquired about the welfare of Vṛṣṇis who sat around him (स तान् अभ्यर्च्य मेधावी पृष्ट्वा च कुशलं तदा) 14. 58. 17-19; (53) On hearing the war account from Kṛṣṇa, Vṛṣṇis experienced the feelings of grief, pain, as well as delight (दुःखहर्षपरिक्लेशा वृष्णीनाम् अभवंस् तदा) 14. 59. 36; (54) Kṛṣṇa, along with Vṛṣṇis, went to Hāstina-pura for the horse sacrifice; when Vṛṣṇi heroes lived there, Parikṣit was born, Abhimanyu had told Uttarā that her son would learn from Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas the science of archery, the different अस्त्रस्, and the entire science of morals (गत्वा वृष्ण्यन्धककुलं धनुर्वेदं ग्रही-ष्यति । अस्त्राणि च विचित्राणि नीतिशास्त्रं च केवलम् ॥ ) 14. 65. 1, 8, 24; (55) When Parikṣit was restored to life by Kṛṣṇa, Vṛṣṇi chiefs (वृष्णिशार्दूलाः) gave Uttarā many jewels as gift; when Pāṇḍavas arrived at the place where Parikṣit was born, Vṛṣṇi chiefs (वृष्णिपुंगवाः) came out to welcome them (14. 69. 8-9, 13); Pāṇḍavas, along with Vṛṣṇis (वृष्णिभिः सह), entered Hāstinapura; when Vyāsa arrived, Kuru chiefs (Pāṇḍavas) sat near him along with Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka heroes (सह वृष्ण्यन्धकव्याघ्रैः) 14. 70. 2, 11; (56) The Aśvamedha horse went to Dvāravatī which was protected by Vṛṣṇi heroes (वृष्णिवीर-) 14. 84. 13; when the horse sacrifice was in progress, Kṛṣṇa, with Vṛṣṇis reached Hāstinapura 14. 88. 4; (57) Yudhiṣṭhira told Kuntī that only the Vṛṣṇi circle (वृष्णिचक्रम्) had survived the war due to the favour of Kṛṣṇa 15. 44. 34; (58) Janamejaya asked Vaiśaṃpāyana how were Andhakas, Vṛṣṇis and Bhojas destroyed in the presence of Vāsudeva and who pronounced the curse on them due to which they perished 16. 2. 1, 3; Vaiśaṃpāyana then told him that thirtysix years (after the coronation of Yudhiṣṭhira) Vṛṣṇis misbehaved and, as dictated by Kāla, they killed each other with pestle; the sages (Viśvāmitra, Kaṇva and Nārada) pronounced a curse to the effect that Sāmba would give birth to an iron pestle for the destruction of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas (वृष्ण्य्-अन्धकविनाशाय); that pestle would wipe out the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas who were ill-behaved, cruel and naughty, and the entire race except Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa (येन यूयं सुदुर्वृत्ता नृशंसा जातमन्य-वः । उच्छेत्तारः कुलं कृत्स्नम् ऋते राम-जनार्दनौ); when Kṛṣṇa heard what had happened, he told Vṛṣṇis that the curse would prove true (भवितव्यं तथा) 16. 2. 2, 8-9, 13; the next day Sāmba gave birth to a pestle for the destruction of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas; when the matter was reported to Ugrasena he prohibited fer-mentation of liquor in all the houses of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas (अद्यप्रभृति सर्-वेषु वृष्ण्यन्धकगृहेष्व् इह । सुरासवो न कर्तव्यः सर्वैर् नगरवासिभिः ॥ ) 16. 2. 15, 18; (59) When Vṛṣṇis and Andha-kas were trying to protect themselves, Kāla constantly visited their houses; a certain bald, fierce man surveyed their houses and disappeared; day after day strong winds blew to foretell the de-struction of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas; day and night, सारिकास् produced shrill, unceasing sounds in the houses of Vṛṣṇis; pale pigeons with red feet, inspired by Kāla, moved in the houses of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas; there occurred many other bad omens; asses with shrill voices responded to the sound pro-duced by Pāñcajanya (एवं प्रयतमाना-नां वृष्णीनाम् अन्धकैः सह । कालो गृहाणि सर्वेषां परिचक्राम नित्यशः; पाण्डुरा रक्तपादाश् च विहगाः कालचोदिताः । वृष्ण्य्-अन्धकानां गेहेषु कपोता व्यचरंस् तदा; नदन्तं पाञ्चजन्यं च वृष्ण्यन्धक-निवेशने । समन्तात् प्रत्यवाश्यन्त रासभा दारुणस्वराः ॥ ) 16. 3. 1-7, 10-15; Vṛṣṇis, except Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, were not ashamed to commit sins; the rest hated Brāhmaṇas, fore-fathers and gods, disrespected elders in general; women and men transgressed rules of morality (पत्न्यः पतीन् व्युच्च-रन्त पत्नीश् च पतयस् तथा) 16. 3. 8-9; (60) Vṛṣṇi women dreamt at night that a black woman with white teeth, laughing, ran around Dvārakā robbing them and men dreamt that fierce demons deprived them of their ornaments, छत्रस् flag-staffs and armours; the चक्र given to Kṛṣṇa by Agni rose up to the sky within the sight of Vṛṣṇis (वृष्णीनां पश्यताम्); the four horses took the chariot upwards and the Apsarases took away, day and night, the flag-staffs of Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa and asked Vṛṣṇis to proceed on a तीर्थ-यात्रा 16. 4. 1-5; (61) The great Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka heroes desired to go for a तीर्थयात्रा along with their women; they took with them eatables (meat) and drinks (liquors) of different kinds and set out of the city 16. 4. 6-8; (62) Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka heroes, overpowered by Kāla, saw Uddhava deserting them; Kṛṣṇa knew the iminent destruction of Vṛṣṇis and hence he did not object to Uddhava's leaving Vṛṣṇis (कालपरीतास् ते वृष्ण्य्-अन्धकमहारथाः) 16. 4. 11-12; (63) Goaded by Kāla, Andhakas, Bhojas, Śaine-yas and Vṛṣṇis struck one another with the दर्भस् turned into pestles 16. 4. 36 (cf. 16. 4. 34-35); (64) Brooding over the destruction of Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, Kṛṣṇa thought it was time for him to depart (स चिन्तयानो ऽन्धकवृष्णिनाशम् … मेने ततः संक्रमणस्य कालम्) 16. 5. 18; (65) Dāruka went to Kurus (i. e. Pāṇḍa-vas) and reported to them the mutual killings of Vṛṣṇis with pestles (आचष्ट मौ-सले वृष्णीन् अन्योन्येनोपसंहृतान्) 16. 6. 1; (66) Yudhiṣṭhira heard the destruction of the Vṛṣṇi clan (शुश्राव वृष्णिचक्रस्य मौसले कदनं कृतम्) 16. 1. 7; Pāṇḍa-vas grieved to hear the destruction of Vṛṣṇis (Vārṣṇeyas) due to their attacking one another (परस्परं समासाद्य … वृष्णीन् विनष्टांश् … ) 16. 1. 9; (विन-ष्टान् वार्ष्णेयान् सभोजकुकुरान्धकान्) 16. 6. 2; (67) Arjuna saw Dvārakā in the form of a river which was once full of water in the form of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas but now bereft of Vṛṣṇi chiefs (तां स वृष्ण्यन्धकजलाम् … द्वारका-सरितं … विहीनां वृष्णिपुंगवैः) 16. 6. 8, 10-11; (68) Kṛṣṇa had asked Vasu-deva to inform Arjuna on his arrival at Dvārakā about the calamity that overtook Vṛṣṇis (वृष्णीनां वैशसं महत्) 16. 7. 14; (69) Vasudeva told Arjuna that Vṛṣṇis were destroyed due to the miscon-duct of Pradyumna and Sātyaki; the two started the destruction of Vṛṣṇis (तयोर् अपनयात् पार्थ वृष्णयो निधनं गताः ।  … प्रद्युम्नो युयुधानश् च … । … ताव् उभौ वृष्णिनाशस्य मुखम् आस्ताम्) 16. 7. 5-7; (70) Arjuna told Vasudeva that he would take with him the women of Vṛṣṇīs as well as their old men and children (वृष्णिदारांस् तु बालवृद्धांस् तथैव च); he informed Dāruka that he would like to meet the ministers of Vṛṣṇi heroes (अमात्यान् वृष्णिवीराणाम्); he assured the gathering assembled in the Sudharmā Hall that he himself would take with him the Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka people to Indraprastha (अहं नेष्ये वृष्ण्यन्धक-जनं स्वयम्) 16. 8. 5, 6, 10; (71) Before departure, young Vṛṣṇi princes, led by Vajra, and the women offered oblations of water to Vasudeva (ततो वज्रप्रधानास् ते वृष्णिवीरकुमारकाः । सर्व एवोदकं चक्रुः स्त्रियश् चैव महात्मनः ॥ ); then Arjuna went to the place where Vṛṣṇis were destroyed; he was grieved to see them dead and did whatever was necessary on that occasion (प्राप्तकालं चकार च) 16. 8. 27-29; (72) On the seventh day after the funeral rites of Vasudeva and others, Arjuna started for Indraprastha; Vṛṣṇi women, weeping and grieved, followed him in carriages drawn by horses, bulls, asses and camels (पाण्डवः । सप्तमे दिवसे प्रायाद् … अश्वयुक्तैर् रथैश् चापि गोखरोष्ट्रयुतैर् अपि । स्त्रियस् ता वृष्णि-वीराणाम् … अनुजग्मुर् … ॥ ); he was also followed by the servants of Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, as well as, by horse-riders, chari-oteers, and those riding elephants along with their foot-guards armed with exce-llent weapons (कुञ्जरैश् च गजारोहा ययुः … सपादरक्षैः संयुक्ताः सोत्तरा-युधिका ययुः); citizens, young and old, including sons of Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, all the four castes and their women followed him; sixteen thousand wives of Vāsudeva (Kṛṣṇa) left Dvārakā following Vajra (दश षट् च सहस्राणिवासुदे वावरोध-नम्); the number of Bhoja, Andhaka, and Vṛṣṇi women who had lost their husbands was extremely large (बहूनि च सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्य् अर्बुदानि च । भोजवृष्ण्यन्धक-स्त्रीणां हतनाथानि निर्ययुः ॥ ); the large number of prosperous Vṛṣṇi people looked like an ocean (तत् सागरसमप्रख्यं वृष्णिचक्रं महर्धिमत्); when those dwellers of Dvārakā left, the city was plunged in waters of ocean; the citizens left in great hurry crying ‘oh! this was our Fate!’ (तूर्णात् तूर्णतरम् जग्मुर् अहो दैवम् इति ब्रुवन् ॥ ) 16. 8. 32-41; (73) While Arjuna was taking Vṛṣṇis and their women with him, in Pañca-nada they were attacked by Ābhīras (Dasyus) in order to deprive them of their wealth (अभ्यधावन्त वृष्णीनां तं जनं लोप्त्रहारिणः … अभिपेतुर् धना-र्थं ते) 16. 8. 42-48; Vṛṣṇi warriors, riding elephants, horses and chariots, were unable to check the robbers carrying away Vṛṣṇi women; Arjuna tried to protect the large number of women running in different directions (कलत्रस्य बहुत्वात् तु सं-पतत्सु ततस् ततः); the excellent women were dragged away in the presence of all warriors; but some went willingly (प्रम-दोत्तमाः । समन्ततो ऽवकृष्यन्त कामाच् चान्याः प्रवव्रजुः) 16. 8. 42, 47, 55-57; (74) Then Arjuna, helped by Vṛṣṇi ser-vants, struck Dasyus with arrows (शरैः पार्थो … । जघान दस्यून् … वृष्णिभृत्यैः सह प्रभुः ॥ ); excellent women of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas were abducted by Mlecchas in spite of Arjuna (प्रेक्षतस् त्व् एव पार्थस्य वृष्ण्यन्धकवरस्त्रियः । जग्मुर् आदाय ते म्लेच्छाः ॥ ); the few women of Vṛṣṇīs who escaped were taken by Arjuna to Kurukṣetra and he settled them there at various places (ततः स शेषम् आदाय कलत्रस्य महामतिः । हृतभूयिष्ठरत्नस्य कुरुक्षेत्रम् अवा-तरत् । एवं कलत्रम् आनीय वृष्णीनां हृतशेषितम् । न्यवेशयत कौरव्यस् तत्र तत्र धनंजयः ॥ ) 16. 8. 58, 61, 65-66; (75) Arjuna informed Vyāsa about the destruction of Vṛṣṇi heroes at Prabhāsa caused by the curse of Brāhmaṇas; five hundred thousand brave Bhoja, Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka warriors had killed one another with एरका grass; he also told him that thousands of Vṛṣṇi women were abducted by Ābhīras of Pañcanada in spite of him (हतं पञ्चशतं तेषां सहस्रं (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 16. 8. 11: पञ्चशतं सहस्रं सहस्रगुणितं पञ्चलक्षानीत्य् अर्थः); वृष्णिदाराश् च … सहस्रशः । आभीरैर् … हृताः पञ्चनदालयैः हृताः) 16. 9. 8-11, 16; (76) Vyāsa consoled Arjuna by saying that the great warriors of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas were burnt by the curse of Brāhmaṇas and therefore Arjuna should not be grieved over their destruction; what had happened was bound to happen for that was dictated by fate for the magnanimous (Vṛṣṇis) (भवितव्यं तथा तद् धि दिष्टम् एतन् महात्मनाम्) 16. 9. 25-26; (77) Arjuna reported to Yudhiṣṭhira exactly what had happened to Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka people (आचष्ट तद् यथावृत्तम्) 16. 9. 38; (78) Janamejaya asked Vaiśaṃpāyana what the Pāṇḍavas did after hearing about the strife in the family of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas (वृष्ण्यन्-धककुले … आहवम्); Vaiśaṃpāyana told him that having heard about the great destruction of Vṛṣṇis (वृष्णीनां कदनं महत्), Yudhiṣṭhira decided to leave the kingdom (to retire to the forest); consi-dering the destruction of Vṛṣṇis and know-ing the decision of Yudhiṣṭhira, all his brothers were glad to follow him (हर्षो ऽभवच् च सर्वेषां भ्रातॄणां गमनं प्रति । युधिष्ठिरमतं ज्ञात्वा वृष्णि-क्षयम् अवेक्ष्य च) 17. 1. 1-2, 22; (79) In heaven, Yudhiṣṭhira was shown great heroes of Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas (वृष्ण्यन्धक-महारथान्) among the groups of Sādhyas, Vasus and Maruts 18. 4. 14. वेणिक: Veṇika m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the second day of the war, Veṇika warriors with their armies led by Duḥ-śāsana, Vikarṇa and others were among those who were expected to protect Bhīṣma in the Mahāvyūha of Kauravas (वेणिकाः कुकुरास् तथा । … भीष्मम् एवाभि-रक्षन्तु सह सैन्यपुरस्कृताः ॥ ; अव्यू-हन्त महाव्यूहम्) 6. 47. 7, 9-10.
वेणुप: Veṇupa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Kṛṣṇa told Karṇa that if he joined the side of Pāṇḍavas, Veṇupas would be among those who would lead his procession (पुरोगमाश् च ते सन्तु … चूचुपा वेणुपास् तथा) 5. 138. 25.
वेणुमण्डल: Veṇumaṇḍala nt. (sg.): Name of a Varṣa. Second among the seven Varṣas of the Kuśadvīpa which is to the north of the Jambudvīpa (उत्तरेषु … द्वीपेषु … । … द्वितीयं वेणुमण्डलम्) 6. 13. 1, 12; for the characteristics common to all Varṣas of Kuśadvīpa, see Audbhida2.
वैयमक: Vaiyamaka m. (pl.): Name of a people. Described as brave (शूर); mentioned by Duryodhana among Kāyavyas, Daradas, Dārvas and others whose kings brought wealth by hundreds as their tribute for the Rājaśūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (कायव्या दरदा दार्वाः शूरा वैयमकास् तथा; आहार्षुः क्षत्रिया वित्तं शतशो ऽजातशत्रवे) 2. 48. 12, 16.
वैराम: Vairāma m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: They were born in the bay (?) of the (western) ocean, near the river Sindhu (समुद्रनिष्कुटे जाताः परि-सिन्धु च मानवाः) 2. 47. 9 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 11: समुद्रसमी-पस्थनिष्कुटे गृहोद्याने). B. Characte-ristics: They lived on grains which grew of their own accord or which they culti-vated using river water (इन्द्रकृष्टैर् वर्त-यन्ति धान्यैर् नदीमुखैश् च ये) 2. 47. 9 (For Nīlakaṇṭha's comment see Pārada p. 783). C. Epic event: They brought tribute for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya many kinds of articles and jewels of various types (वीविधं बलिम् आदाय रत्नानि विविधानि च), but they were stopped at the gate (ते वैरामाः … । … द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः) 2. 47. 10-11 (the details of the tribute are given in 2. 47. 11 for which see Pārada).
